summary: Lipnowski and Tsimerman count abelian varieties over a prime field F_p as g→∞. Isogeny classes number q^((1/4)g²(1+o(1))) (Lemma 2.1 corrected, with DiPippo–Howe). Each isogeny class is a class set of Frobenius-stable lattices, bounded locally with Yun's Hilbert-scheme count and globally with class numbers, giving log B(p,g) = O_p(g²) (Theorem 0.1). The printed exponent 17/2 is not established: the corrected argument gives 2^(34g²)p^((69/4)g²) (Lee 2022). Principal polarizations are Rosati orbits of positive symmetric units; E^g carries exp((1/2)g² log g) of them (Lemma 5.11, printed coefficient 1), so most ppavs have repeated factors (Theorem 0.3). Assuming a model-ring conjecture, a factor E^h or, as corrected here, B0^(h/2) with h ≥ 0.99g is typical (Theorem 0.2), with consequences for random-matrix and Cohen–Lenstra heuristics. The atlas lacks Honda–Tate theory, finite-field lattice counting and polarization counting: these form a Part II of Abelian Schemes and Arithmetic Moduli; hermitian masses go to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2–GN.3, level maps to AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4, Dieudonné inputs to R07.2, and the statistics to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.5. Twenty-two findings are recorded, five already corrected in Lee 2022.

items.name: Abelian variety over a field
items.statement: An abelian variety over k is a proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec k; its dimension is the Krull dimension of its underlying scheme. Smoothness and geometric connectedness are derived.
items.note: API: Reuse the bundled carrier, Hom/End, products, field extension and dimension; prove finite natural dimension before using g in counts. Tests: (1) the zero variety has dimension zero; (2) geometric connectedness is required; (3) the finite-field model is not an abstract finite abelian group.

items.name: Unweighted abelian-variety count
items.statement: B(p,g) is the number of F_p-isomorphism classes of g-dimensional abelian varieties over the prime field F_p, for fixed prime p and g tending to infinity.
items.note: API: Construct the isomorphism quotient, finite cardinality after its finiteness theorem, and decomposition over isogeny classes. Tests: (1) isogenous nonisomorphic varieties remain distinct; (2) automorphism orders do not weight this count; (3) p stays fixed in every g-asymptotic.

items.name: Unweighted principally polarized count
items.statement: A(p,g) counts F_p-isomorphism classes of pairs (A,λ) with dim A=g and λ a principal polarization; equivalences preserve λ. The associated distribution is uniform on these classes.
items.note: API: Use polarization-preserving isomorphisms, forgetful fibers and finite probability measures; distinguish stack mass and coarse rational points. Tests: (1) one A can give several classes; (2) a twist can share a coarse moduli point; (3) sum 1/|Aut(A,λ)| is a different quantity.

items.name: Number of polarizations on a fixed variety
items.statement: n_A is the number of Aut_k(A)-orbits on principal polarizations of A, and is zero if A has none.
items.note: API: Define fibers of the forgetful class map; prove A(p,g)=Σ_[A] n_A only after finiteness; guard log n_A by n_A>0. Tests: (1) an empty polarization set gives zero; (2) changing an isomorphic underlying representative preserves n_A; (3) counting line bundles would overcount Pic⁰ translates. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Theorem 0.1, corrected: abelian varieties over F_p number p^(O(g²))
items.statement: Fix a prime p and let B(p,g) be the number of isomorphism classes of g-dimensional abelian varieties over F_p. Then log B(p,g) = O_p(g²). Explicitly, the paper's argument with the corrections of Lee 2022 §3.1 gives B(p,g) ≤ 2^(34g²)·p^((69/4)g²(1+o(1))) as g→∞ (Lee, Theorem 1.1), and Lee's refinement gives B(p,g) ≤ p^((45/4)g²(1+o(1))) (Lee, Theorem 1.4). The printed bound B(p,g) = o_ε(p^((17/2+ε)g²)) is not established (E21).
items.note: Corrected statement (PROTOCOL §18). The printed exponent 17/2 = 1/4 + 33/4 comes from (28), which undercounts ordered root pairs in (14) and (20) (E19), halves the class-group exponent in (26)–(27) (E6, E20) and drops powers of 2 with exponent of order g² (E7). Lee 2022 corrects the first three and keeps the power of 2. The v1 local-counting steps (13) and §3.2.1 have further failing steps (E1–E4), which the published version may already revise (Lee quotes a different local count from published p.3421); the replacement items repeated-block-orbit-bound, adelic-local-orbit-bound, nonisotypic-stabilizer-bound and conditional-rational-orbit-bound are what the design job proves. For comparison Lee, Theorem 1.2 gives B(p,g) ≥ p^((1/2)g²(1+o(1))). Routed to the finite-field Part II as its main theorem. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G0/G1/G2: recorded source claim, not an accepted numerical target. Equations (26)–(28) lose discriminant squares and fixed-p powers of 2; the exact exponent needs the final paper and a repaired local argument. Unrouted.

items.name: Theorem 0.3 (Proposition 4.17): most ppavs over F_p have a repeated factor
items.statement: Let p be a prime satisfying the corrected conclusion of Lemma 5.11 (for instance, p splits in one of the nine imaginary quadratic fields of class number one). Among isomorphism classes of g-dimensional principally polarized abelian varieties over F_p, the proportion whose underlying abelian variety has no repeated F_p-simple isogeny factor and has Frobenius characteristic polynomial coprime to x²−p tends to 0 as g→∞.
items.note: The statement survives the corrections: Proposition 4.16 with Corollary 2.2 and the per-isogeny-class bound gives at most p^(O(g²)) such ppavs (the constants change by E6, E7, E19, E20 but stay O_p(g²)), while E^g alone carries exp((1/2)g² log g + O_p(g²)) principal polarizations (elliptic-power-source, corrected by E13). Routed to the finite-field Part II. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G0/G4: retain the conjunction and the prime restriction. The qualitative comparison exp(O_p(g²)) versus exp(c g² log g) is the mechanism; quantitative suppliers are not closed. Unrouted pending source reconciliation.

items.name: Theorem 0.2 (Corollary 5.13), corrected: a large elliptic or B0 factor, conditionally
items.statement: Let p satisfy the corrected conclusion of Lemma 5.11. Assume Conjecture 5.2 and its analogue for abelian varieties with isogeny factors B0 (the simple abelian surface over F_p with Frobenius ±√p, whose endomorphism algebra is the definite quaternion algebra over Q(√p)). Then the proportion of g-dimensional principally polarized abelian varieties over F_p whose underlying variety has an isogeny factor E^h, with E/F_p elliptic, or B0^(h/2), for some h ≥ 0.99g, tends to 1 as g→∞. The printed form (an elliptic factor, assuming Conjecture 5.2 alone) is not established (E14).
items.note: Corrected statement, derived in this extraction (E13, E14); the design job must re-derive it. Conjecture 5.2 only covers isogeny classes whose simple factors have CM-field endomorphism algebras. For B0^n the model count is a mass of quaternion-hermitian lattices with leading term 2n² log n = (1/2)(2n)² log n, the same coefficient per dimension as E^g, so B0-heavy classes cannot be discarded. With the factor 1/2 of E13 in both (55) and Lemma 5.11, the threshold of Proposition 5.10 becomes 0.495g² log g and the conclusion keeps h ≥ 0.99g. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.5. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G4/G5: Conjecture 5.2 only covers products of CM-field matrix algebras; the real-Weil/quaternionic factor is not covered. The coefficient 0.99 also depends on the disputed mass asymptotic. Unrouted.

items.name: Compactly supported trace formula
items.statement: For a separated finite-type scheme X/F_q and ℓ∤q, #X(F_q)=Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(Frob_q | H_c^i(X_bar,Q_ℓ)), with geometric Frobenius convention.
items.note: Planned: WeilConjectures WC.0 reconciles the point-counting and trace-formula owners that WC.1 consumes, and EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.8 states that ordinary Frobenius point counting is "PR196 TraceFormula's theorem" in that campaign. Section 1 is motivation and is not used in §§2–5. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: The paper explicitly suppresses stack issues. This item is scheme-valued only; no unweighted stack count follows.

items.name: Weights used in the point-count heuristic
items.statement: The source uses |α|≤q^(i/2) for eigenvalues on H_c^i of a smooth F_q-variety; purity of weight i requires properness as well.
items.note: DWP.7 and its reviewed audit read: the upper compact-support bound and smooth proper purity are existing targets. This motivational input is not used in §§2–5; no purity claim for arbitrary open varieties.

items.name: Isogeny of abelian varieties
items.statement: An isogeny is a group-scheme homomorphism whose underlying scheme map is finite and surjective; inseparability is allowed.
items.note: API: Reuse IsIsogeny, composition, invariance under isomorphism and base change; rationalize Hom separately. Tests: (1) identity is an isogeny; (2) inseparable Frobenius is not excluded; (3) finite alone does not supply surjectivity.

items.name: Rational endomorphism algebra
items.statement: End⁰_k(A)=End_k(A)⊗_Z Q; quasi-isogenies are its units for self-maps, and invertible morphisms in the rationalized category for different varieties.
items.note: API: Extend the existing End ring by rational scalar extension; prove inverse denominators, composition and centralizers. Tests: (1) [m] for m≠0 becomes invertible; (2) integral automorphisms form a smaller subgroup; (3) base-field endomorphisms need not be geometric endomorphisms.

items.name: Isogeny decomposition and semisimplicity
items.statement: Over a field, every abelian variety is isogenous to a product of powers of pairwise nonisogenous simple abelian varieties; its rational endomorphism algebra is the corresponding product of matrix algebras over division algebras.

items.name: Prime-to-characteristic Tate module
items.statement: For ℓ≠char k, T_ℓ(A)=lim_n A[ℓ^n](k_sep) with multiplication-by-ℓ transitions; V_ℓ(A)=T_ℓ(A)⊗Q_ℓ, carrying G_k-action.
items.note: API: Construct the inverse limit and Galois action; prove rank 2g, functoriality, and integral versus rational comparisons. Tests: (1) ℓ=p is excluded here; (2) isogenies act invertibly on V but not always T; (3) a rank-2g statement requires the torsion theorem.

items.name: Tate full faithfulness over finite fields
items.statement: For A,B/F_q and ℓ≠p, Hom_Fq(A,B)⊗Z_ℓ→Hom_Gal(T_ℓA,T_ℓB) is an isomorphism; rationalizing gives the analogous Q_ℓ statement.
items.note: The full Tate 1966 text is now read. C1 expands Proposition 1, Proposition 2, the characteristic-polynomial dimension argument and the integral-saturation step. The A2/A3/PEL geometric supplier interiors and the simple-polynomial Hom-dimension assembly remain G8 leaves; no implementation is claimed. A4 supplies Tate modules, not this theorem.
items.proof: For E=End⁰(A) the central Frobenius algebra Q[π] is finite étale. Choose ℓ split completely in it (a split-prime existence supplier, not the quantitative density item below). The split-commutant lemma proves rational full faithfulness there. Semisimple polynomial modules with characteristic multiplicities a_P,b_P have intertwiner dimension Σ_P a_P b_P deg P; factoring after any characteristic-zero field extension leaves the sum unchanged. Tate Lemma 2 transfers the equality of dimensions to every ℓ≠p; A×B gives Hom from End. The integral map is injective with saturated image: if a homomorphism kills A[ℓ], it factors through [ℓ]. Equal rank and saturation give the integral isomorphism.

items.name: Frobenius polynomial and reciprocity
items.statement: For A/F_q of dimension g, P_A(X)=det(X−Frob_q|V_ℓA) is a monic polynomial in Z[X] of degree 2g, independent of ℓ, with all complex roots of absolute value √q and coefficients satisfying a_(2g−i)=q^(g−i)a_i.
items.note: API: Define from the characteristic polynomial, then prove integrality, independence, multiplicativity and reciprocal symmetry. Tests: (1) P_(A×B)=P_A P_B; (2) constant coefficient is q^g; (3) X²−q satisfies the root-radius condition but not this reciprocal condition. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Frobenius polynomial determines the isogeny class
items.statement: Two abelian varieties over F_q are F_q-isogenous exactly when their Frobenius characteristic polynomials agree.
items.note: Use semisimplicity plus Tate full faithfulness, not only equality of eigenvalue sets. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Honda–Tate simple isogeny classification
items.statement: Simple F_q-isogeny classes correspond to conjugacy classes of q-Weil algebraic integers π. The dimension is determined by 2 dim A=[Q(π):Q] sqrt([End⁰(A):Q(π)]), with the division-algebra local invariants prescribed by π.
items.note: G8: original Honda/Tate statements and local invariants still to extract atomically. This is a supplier target, not permission to regard every degree-2g Weil polynomial as realized by dimension g. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Lemma 2.1, corrected: counting Weil polynomials
items.statement: For q≥2 and g≥1, the number of monic reciprocal integer polynomials of degree 2g with constant q^g and all roots of absolute value √q is at most (4g+1)^g q^(g(g+1)/4).
items.note: The k-th power sum is an integer of absolute value ≤2g q^(k/2); its possible values number at most (4g+1)q^(k/2). The first g power sums determine the first g coefficients by Newton identities; reciprocity determines the rest. This is an explicitly derived replacement, not the printed constant. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports. Lemma 2.1 as printed ((2g)^g q^(g(g+1)/4), without reciprocity) is recorded in E5; this item is its corrected statement and replaces the withheld literal item power-sum-source. [cc-442dc5]

items.name: Asymptotic count of isogeny classes
items.statement: For fixed q, the number of dimension-g F_q-isogeny classes is at most exp((log q)g²/4+O_q(g log g)).
items.note: Only injectivity of the class-to-polynomial map is used. No Honda–Tate surjectivity onto all polynomials is needed. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Frobenius isocrystal carrier
items.statement: Over a perfect field k of characteristic p, an F-isocrystal is a vector space over Frac W(k) with a bijective Witt-Frobenius-semilinear map.
items.note: API: Import the existing carrier, Frobenius and equivariant homomorphisms; impose finite dimension explicitly. Tests: (1) over F_p the coefficient Frobenius is identity; (2) over F_(p^r) semilinearity is retained; (3) an arbitrary linear map is not an isocrystal morphism.

items.name: Integral Dieudonné realization
items.statement: For A/F_q, the chosen covariant Dieudonné module D₀(A) is a free W(F_q)-module of rank 2g with F,V semilinear in opposite directions and FV=VF=p; D(A)=D₀(A)[1/p].
items.note: API: Import R07.2 with one fixed covariance convention; prove isogeny transport, F/V stability and recovery of p-power subgroup quotients. Tests: (1) F and V are Q_p-linear only over F_p; (2) rank counts height rather than dimension of A[p](k_bar); (3) changing covariance reverses the quasi-isogeny lattice map. C3 fixes the prime-field application explicitly as D^lin₀=Hom_Zp(C,Z_p), with transposed F,V and π_D=F_D. This is not silently identified with an arbitrary general-q covariant/Cartier-dual convention.

items.name: Prime-to-p and p lattice spaces
items.statement: X^p is the restricted product of Frob-stable full Z_ℓ-lattices in V_ℓ(A₀), equal to T_ℓ(A₀) almost everywhere; X_p is the set of W(F_q)-lattices in D(A₀) stable under both F and V.
items.note: API: Define restricted support, full lattices and rational-centralizer actions, with a separate p component. Tests: (1) a collection modified at infinitely many primes is excluded; (2) F-stability alone is insufficient at p; (3) endomorphism units preserve the stability predicates. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Marked quasi-isogenies classified by lattices
items.statement: Isomorphism classes of pairs (A,f:A→A₀ a rational quasi-isogeny) correspond to X_p×X^p via covariant realization transport.
items.note: G8: construction requires Tate and Dieudonné full faithfulness and finite-flat quotients. Do not infer essential surjectivity merely from the linear maps. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports. C4 now supplies its prime-field restriction in prime-field-marked-classification using actual finite-flat quotient construction and torsion detection, without invoking full Tate faithfulness. General-q covariance and proof closure remain open.

items.name: Isomorphism classes as rational orbits
items.statement: The underlying F_q-isomorphism classes in the isogeny class of A₀ are End⁰(A₀)^×\(X_p×X^p).
items.note: Changing the marking acts by postcomposition. Global rational orbits differ from independent local orbits. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports. C4 now proves the prime-field action/quotient comparison in prime-field-marked-classification; no all-q closure is claimed.

items.name: The prime-field p-component reduction
items.statement: For A₀/F_p, F is Q_p-linear and V=pF^(−1); hence the simultaneous centralizer of F,V is the centralizer of F, and its orbits on F,V-stable lattices form a subset of its orbits on F-stable lattices.
items.note: For F_(p^r), r>1, the coefficient Frobenius is nontrivial; this argument does not extend by replacing p with q. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports. C3 uses D^lin and p-tate-hom to identify the arithmetic group with this linear centralizer; prime-field-p-frobenius separately supplies the common semisimple Frobenius polynomial.

items.name: Local monogenic order
items.statement: For a monic irreducible f∈Z_ℓ[X] with separable fraction algebra F, R=Z_ℓ[X]/(f)⊂O_F; an R-lattice of rank n is a full Z_ℓ-lattice in F^n stable under R.
items.note: API: Use existing submodules, integral closure and finite-length quotients; define saturation and the trace-dual lattice. Tests: (1) R=O_F gives one GL_n(F)-orbit of R-lattices; (2) nonmaximal orders allow nonfree modules; (3) the residue field of R need not equal F_ℓ. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports. Continuation: reuse Mathlib Submodule.traceDual / the trace-form dualSubmodule for ordinary trace duality; do not define a competing dual-lattice carrier.

items.name: Normalized lattice sandwiches
items.statement: For an R-lattice M⊂F^n, some g∈GL_n(F) puts it in R^n⊂gM⊂O_F^n.
items.note: First normalize O_F M to O_F^n. Choose n elements of M whose reductions form a residue-field basis and use Nakayama to obtain an O_F-basis. The next passage to sublattices of R^n needs a separate duality argument, G2. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Stable lattice with prescribed flag quotients
items.statement: For semisimple γ preserving 0⊂V₁⊂V and V₂=V/V₁, fix full γ-stable lattices U₁⊂V₁,U₂⊂V₂. Consider full γ-stable L⊂V with L∩V₁=U₁ and image U₂.
items.note: API: Construct the fiber and equivariant splitting; encode it by γ-equivariant maps U₂→V₁/U₁. Tests: (1) projection to V₂ is not intersection with a chosen V₂ summand; (2) a split lattice gives the zero extension; (3) equal eigenvalues require quotienting by shears. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Centralizer shears identify equivalent extensions
items.statement: Two such lattices whose maps U₂→V₁/U₁ differ by a rational γ-equivariant map U₂→V₁ lie in the same centralizer orbit.
items.note: Choose a γ-equivariant splitting. The unipotent block matrix with that difference as off-diagonal entry commutes with γ and transports one graph lattice to the other. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Resultant cardinality of a disjoint-spectrum fiber
items.statement: If γ₁ and γ₂ on the two graded spaces have disjoint spectra, the flag fiber has q^(v_F Res(P₁,P₂)) elements, where P_i are their full characteristic polynomials over a local field F with residue size q.
items.note: Yun proof read. The determinant of γ₂*⊗1−1⊗γ₁ gives the exponent. Each unordered pair of blocks occurs once; characteristic-polynomial multiplicities matter. Repeated blocks require the separate shear quotient. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Bound after removing zero eigenspaces
items.statement: For the extension quotient in §3.1.4, semisimplicity bounds its order by the residue cardinality to the valuation of the product of all nonzero cross-eigenvalue differences, counted with multiplicity.
items.note: The cokernel torsion is a quotient of the lattice on the nonzero-eigenvalue subspace modulo F applied to that lattice; the printed subset inclusion is reversed. Prove the quotient map explicitly. This does not certify the later global exponent. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports. Continuation L5 proves the graph/shear quotient is M'/FM, with a canonical surjection M'/FM'→M'/FM. Here W=Hom_K(V₂,V₁), M=Hom_O(U₂,U₁), F(T)=γ₁T−Tγ₂, W'=im F and M'=M∩W'. Semisimplicity gives W=ker F⊕W'. A finite-DVR determinant/index adapter computes #M'/FM'=ℓ^(v_ℓ det(F|W')).

items.name: Finite-colength ideal count
items.statement: For a complete DVR O with residue field F_q, Hilb^j_(O[[X]]) denotes ideals I with O-module length(O[[X]]/I)=j.
items.note: API: Use ideals and module length; classify by initial ideals/partitions and finite residue choices. Tests: (1) j=0 contains the whole ring only; (2) length is measured over O; (3) a residue extension changes q and scales base-ring length. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Yun finite-colength partition formula
items.statement: #Hilb^j_(O[[X]])=Σ_(λ partition of j) q^(j−length λ).
items.note: Full proof read: initial ideals have the same colength, the lifts of I_μ number q^(|μ|−μ₀), then transpose partitions. In particular j=0,1,2 give 1,1,q+1. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Crude partition upper bound
items.statement: For j≥0, #Hilb^j_(O[[X]])≤(2q)^j.
items.note: For j≥1 bound the number of partitions by 2^(j−1), and each exponent by j; handle j=0 separately. A general local order must first be reduced to the same residue field, as Yun Corollary 4.10 does. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Adelic class set of the endomorphism group
items.statement: For G=(End⁰(A₀))^× and an adelic lattice L, the global orbits inside its G(A_fin)-orbit are G(Q)\G(A_fin)/Stab(L).
items.note: API: Construct orbit decomposition and compact-open stabilizers; compare smaller stabilizers with maximal compact opens by index inequalities. Tests: (1) rational orbits need not coincide with adelic orbits; (2) nontrivial stabilizers are retained; (3) an index gives an upper bound without an unjustified free action. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Strong approximation supplier
items.statement: A simply connected almost-simple group over a number field satisfies strong approximation away from a nonempty set S when the relevant S-local group is noncompact, with the standard isotropy/noncompactness hypothesis on each factor.
items.note: AUDIT-09/AA.4 inspected: the library only has a congruence SL₂/Q instance, not the groups used here. The compact definite quaternion norm-one group in rank one is excluded.

items.name: Class-set comparison by reduced norms
items.statement: Let K₀=Q(√p), D₀/K₀ the quaternion algebra ramified at both real places and split at every finite place, and d≥2. With maximal finite compact U₀,d=∏_v GL_(2d)(O_(K₀,v)), reduced norm identifies GL_d(D₀)(K₀)\GL_d(D₀)(A_(K₀,fin))/U₀,d with the narrow ideal class group Cl⁺(K₀). For each CM field K_i, determinant identifies GL_(n_i)(K_i)\GL_(n_i)(A_(K_i,fin))/GL_(n_i)(Ohat_(K_i)) with Cl(K_i). Their product gives the mixed class set. The d=1 quaternion factor remains its own class set; d=0 omits it.
items.note: Explicit corrected supplier target derived from strong approximation and the reduced-norm image theorem, not a verbatim statement of (21). At real ramified places norms are positive; Cl⁺ rather than Cl occurs. Its ratio to Cl is at most 2^[K₀:Q]=4, harmless for fixed-p exponential scale. G8: acquire the original approximation and norm-image proofs; the rank-one finite quaternion class number is separate. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Analytic class number formula
items.statement: For a number field K, lim_(s→1+) (s−1)ζ_K(s)=2^r₁(2π)^r₂ h_K R_K/(w_K√|D_K|).
items.note: The pinned theorem is the real right-hand residue limit. No meromorphic continuation is being claimed by this citation.

items.name: Available uniform class-number bound
items.statement: For every number field K, h_K≤|D_K|·4^[K:Q].
items.note: This already proves the exp(O_p(g²)) scale once the discriminant and dimension sums are bounded; it does not recover the printed 17/2 constant.

items.name: Correct elementary discriminant estimate
items.statement: If K=Q(π), π is an integral p-Weil number of degree d, then |D_K|≤|disc minpoly(π)|≤(2√p)^(d(d−1)).
items.note: The Vandermonde product is squared: ∏_(i<j)|π_i−π_j|². The printed binomial exponent misses this square. Combined with coarse-class-bound and Σd_i≤2g this gives product h_(K_i)≤exp(O_p(g²)). Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Explicit lower bound for regulators (Skoruppa), as quoted
items.statement: The source quotes R_K/w_K≥0.00299 exp(0.48r₁+0.06r₂)≥1/500.
items.note: Planned: Tau Ceti EffectiveBounds Layer 3 plans "explicit lower bounds on the regulator". The constants are as quoted by LT; the original [24] was not read. The library bound h_K ≤ |D_K|·4^[K:Q] (coarse-class-bound) already gives the exp(O_p(g²)) scale, so this input only affects explicit constants. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G8: original Skoruppa source and all low-degree conventions need checking; source-scoped analytic estimate not routed from an unverified quotation. Coarse-class-bound makes it unnecessary for the coarse class-set scale.

items.name: Explicit residue bound for Dedekind zeta functions (Louboutin)
items.statement: For degree d>1 the source quotes Res_(s=1) ζ_K(s)≤(e log|D_K|/(2(d−1)))^(d−1).
items.note: Routed as a source of AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4 (Dedekind analytic interfaces and residue constants). (49) also needs a lower bound for Res_(s=1) ζ_K, for example Stark's effective Brauer–Siegel bounds, to control log L(1, χ_(L/K)) from both sides (E12); AN.4 should supply both directions. The original [18] was not read. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G8: original hypotheses not checked. In §5.4.2 an upper bound for each residue does not bound their ratio from both sides. Unrouted.

items.name: Dual variety and rigidified Poincaré bundle
items.statement: A∨ represents the degree-zero Picard functor of A, with a Poincaré line bundle P_A on A×A∨ rigidified on both zero sections.
items.note: API: Import Picard representability, biduality and the rigidified universal property; prove dual functoriality. Tests: (1) zero parameter gives the trivial rigidified bundle; (2) forgetting rigidifications creates scalar automorphisms; (3) duality reverses composition.

items.name: Polarization as a positive symmetric morphism
items.statement: A polarization λ:A→A∨ is symmetric under biduality and has ample graph pullback (1,λ)*P_A; it is principal when λ is an isomorphism.
items.note: API: Export symmetry, ampleness, isogeny and principal predicates, base change and pullback along homomorphisms. Tests: (1) −λ is not positive for dim A>0; (2) a symmetric isomorphism need not be a polarization; (3) principal means degree one, not merely finite kernel.

items.name: Mumford homomorphism of a line bundle
items.statement: For L on A, the rigidified bundle m*L⊗p₁*L^(−1)⊗p₂*L^(−1) corresponds to φ_L:A→A∨, with φ_L(a)=t_a*L⊗L^(−1).
items.note: API: Construct the actual map from the universal property; prove tensor additivity, Pic⁰ kernel and pullback covariance. Tests: (1) φ_(L⊗M)=φ_L+φ_M; (2) Pic⁰ bundles map to zero; (3) graph pullback has class 2[L], not [L].

items.name: Correct graph-pullback normalization
items.statement: (1,φ_L)*P_A≅[2]*L⊗L^(−2), up to the fixed zero-fiber rigidification; its class in NS(A) is 2[L], and it is ample exactly when L is ample.
items.note: The source equality with L is not literal. Conrad was read completely; no ad hoc change of the principal-polarization definition is made. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Kernel of the Mumford map
items.statement: Two line bundles give the same φ_L exactly when their quotient lies in Pic⁰(A); over an algebraically closed field every symmetric map A→A∨ has such a representation.
items.note: Keep the algebraically closed hypothesis in the original construction. Finite fields use the next descent theorem. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Ample line bundles induce isogenies
items.statement: If L is ample on A over a field, φ_L is an isogeny; a polarization is therefore always an isogeny.

items.name: Line-bundle realization over a finite field
items.statement: For A over a finite field, every symmetric isogeny A→A∨ is φ_L for some line bundle over that field.
items.note: The obstruction is a torsor under A∨ and vanishes by Lang. Use the stated isogeny case from the checked Conrad theorem; no arbitrary-field descent is inferred. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Isomorphism of symmetric morphisms
items.statement: An isomorphism (A,f)→(B,g) is an isomorphism α:A→B with f=α∨ g α.
items.note: API: Define composition and inverse and prove compatibility with pullback of line bundles. Tests: (1) identity preserves f; (2) composition requires contravariant dual order; (3) an unpolarized isomorphism may fail the equation.

items.name: Pullback covariance
items.statement: For a homomorphism α:A→B and a line bundle L on B, φ_(α*L)=α∨ φ_L α.

items.name: Rosati involution
items.statement: For a polarization f, h†=f^(−1) h∨ f is a Q-linear involutive anti-automorphism of End⁰(A); S⁰(A) is its fixed subspace.
items.note: API: Use inverse in the isogeny category, prove (ab)†=b†a† and square identity, and define the symmetric subspace. Tests: (1) scalars are fixed; (2) matrix products reverse order; (3) different polarizations can induce different involutions.

items.name: Rational Néron–Severi space
items.statement: NS(A)_Q=(Pic(A)/Pic⁰(A))⊗Q, with its ample cone in NS(A)_R. Rational endomorphism pullbacks act on this rational space after clearing denominators.
items.note: API: Import Picard quotients and rational scalar extension; distinguish integral classes from rational multiples and the open ample cone from its closure. Tests: (1) half an ample class need not be integral; (2) Pic⁰ twists have the same NS class; (3) zero is nef but not ample in positive dimension. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Normalized Néron–Severi/Rosati map
items.statement: For a principal f=φ_(L₀), define Φ_f:NS(A)_Q→S⁰(A) by [L]↦(1/2)f^(−1)φ_L. Define D_f(a,b)=(a+b)*[L₀]−a*[L₀]−b*[L₀] on rationalized classes.
items.note: The factor 1/2 is retained as in the paper; NS must be rationalized. Polarization-orbit identification below uses f^(−1)λ, not Φ_f without rescaling. API: Prove bilinearity of D_f, the inverse a↦D_f(a,1) on symmetric a, and Φ_f(α*L)=α†Φ_f(L)α. Tests: (1) Φ_f([L₀])=1/2; (2) D_f(1,1)=2[L₀]; (3) rational pullbacks cannot be typed as integral line bundles. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Geometric endomorphism trace
items.statement: t(h) is the trace on V_ℓ(A), equivalently the negative coefficient of X^(2g−1) in det(X−h), extended Q-linearly to End⁰(A).
items.note: API: Prove independence of ℓ, t(1)=2g, cyclicity and product compatibility; compare reduced traces with representation multiplicities. Tests: (1) t([m])=2gm; (2) for End⁰=Q the reduced trace of 1 is 1 but t(1)=2g; (3) cyclicity does not require commutativity.

items.name: Degree characteristic polynomial
items.statement: For an endomorphism h of a g-dimensional abelian variety, det(X−h|V_ℓA) is the degree polynomial deg([X]−h), independent of ℓ; degree on End⁰ extends homogeneously of degree 2g.
items.note: G8: read the original degree-polynomial theorem before implementation; equality means polynomial interpolation, not degree of a morphism over a polynomial-valued point.

items.name: Positive Rosati trace pairing
items.statement: For a polarization f, (a,b)↦t(a†b) is a positive-definite Q-bilinear form on End⁰(A).
items.note: Conrad proof read, via 2g(D^(g−1)·a*D)/(D^g)>0. Positivity of this trace form alone does not characterize polarizations among all symmetric isogenies.

items.name: Ample classes and positive symmetric elements
items.statement: Under the rationalized Φ_f, a symmetric invertible a is in the rational ample cone exactly when its characteristic roots are positive real numbers, equivalently when it is a sum of squares of invertible elements of Q[a].
items.note: Interpret the line-bundle side as a positive rational ample class. Lang original proof and the sums-of-squares implication remain G8. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Real ample-cone matrix description
items.statement: A polarized abelian variety has real endomorphism algebra a product of matrix algebras over R,C,H; under compatible involution identifications its ample cone is a product of positive-definite self-adjoint matrix cones with g*a g action.
items.note: Open cone duality means the interior of the dual of its closed cone. Do not assert literal equality of an open cone with its closed dual. The trace metric can have positive factor weights; an unweighted isometry requires its own normalization. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Polarizations as Rosati-conjugacy orbits
items.statement: For a fixed principal polarization f on A/k, principal polarizations up to Aut_k(A) correspond to Aut_k(A)-orbits of integral units a∈End_k(A) fixed by † and positive in the ample cone, by λ=f a and a↦α†aα.
items.note: Use f^(−1)λ without the 1/2 factor in Φ_f. For finite-field k the line-bundle descent above is available; determinant-one terminology must be interpreted via degree/unit conditions. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: No-CM elliptic-power orbit example
items.statement: If End_k(E)=Z, principal polarizations on E^g correspond to positive-definite symmetric matrices in GL_g(Z) modulo integral congruence.
items.note: This example is over a general field; it does not describe elliptic curves over finite fields. Its printed exp(g² log g) count is withheld with G4. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports. The printed count "≈ exp(g² log g)" should be exp((1/4)g² log g + O(g²)): these orbits are the classes of positive definite unimodular Z-lattices of rank g, whose Siegel mass has logarithm (1/4)g² log g + O(g²) (E13). [cc-442dc5]

items.name: CM field and maximal real subfield
items.statement: A CM field L is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of its maximal totally real subfield K.
items.note: API: Import IsCMField, maximalRealSubfield and degree/place APIs. Tests: (1) Q(i) is CM; (2) a totally real field is excluded; (3) [L:Q]=2[K:Q].

items.name: Intrinsic CM conjugation
items.statement: The nonidentity automorphism of L/K agrees with complex conjugation under every embedding L→C.
items.note: API: Import complexConj and embedding compatibility; use it in matrix adjoints and norm units. Tests: (1) conjugating twice is identity; (2) K is fixed pointwise; (3) conjugation is intrinsic rather than an arbitrary embedding choice.

items.name: Polarizations for a maximal CM endomorphism order
items.statement: If A admits a principal polarization and End(A)=O_L for a CM field L with Rosati conjugation, its principal-polarization classes correspond to O_K^(×,+)/N_(L/K)(O_L^×).
items.note: The base principal polarization and Rosati identification are hypotheses. Norms of field elements and norms of units are different subgroups. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports. The bound (31) uses the Hasse norm theorem (hasse-norm-theorem, planned) and Lemmermeyer's exact sequence (ambiguous-unit-norms). [cc-442dc5]

items.name: Commutative endomorphisms in the nonreal prime-field case
items.statement: If A/F_p is simple and Q(Frob) has no real embedding, End⁰_Fp(A)=Q(Frob) is a CM field.
items.note: Retain both simple and prime-field hypotheses. Supersingular elliptic curves over F_(p²) provide the excluded noncommutative behavior. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports. Original Waterhouse Chapter 2 and Theorem 6.1 read; Tate Bourbaki 352 Theorem 1 invariant formula checked on the rendered page. For a=1 every finite local invariant f_v ord_v(π)/a is integral. With no real place all Brauer invariants vanish, so the division algebra is its CM center. The Brauer classification and the original p-invariant proof remain named G8 inputs. D5 now reads and expands WM71 Part II Theorem 2, so the original p-invariant proof is no longer an unread leaf. Its local cyclic-invariant and global Brauer classification suppliers remain explicit. E18 records the false alternative centralizer sentence in v1; use the valid invariant proof, not that shortcut.

items.name: Realization of nonreal prime-field orders
items.statement: In the preceding simple F_p-isogeny class, every order R in Q(Frob) containing Frob and p/Frob occurs as End_Fp(A′) for some A′ in that class.
items.note: Original Waterhouse Theorem 6.1 and Porism 4.3, including their proofs, are now read. At ℓ≠p choose a rank-one R_ℓ-lattice; at p use F=π and V=pπ^(−1) on the rank-one E_p-space. Modify only finitely many places and use C4’s realization; torsion detection identifies the resulting integral endomorphism order as R. In the D^lin convention choose the linear dual of Waterhouse’s contravariant R_p-lattice, not an unjustified identical lattice. No universal order-realization theorem over F_q is asserted. The kernel-ideal classification in 6.1(3) needs a specially chosen locally free reference variety; general lattices of multiplier order R need not be projective and are not all Pic(R). G8 supplier interiors remain.

items.name: Squarefree nonreal polarization bound
items.statement: For A/F_p of dimension g with no repeated simple isogeny factor and P_A coprime to X²−p, the source proves n_A≪p^(C g²) for some absolute C.
items.note: G8: unit norms, nonmaximal-order index and global class-set estimates remain dependencies. The proof only needs an exp(O_p(g²)) scale; no sharpened numerical coefficient is exported. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports. Uses positive-involution-cm for the Rosati involution and the corrected exponents E19–E20; still p^(O(g²)). [cc-442dc5]

items.name: Model ring with positive involution
items.statement: For distinct CM fields L_i with real subfields K_i and n_i>0 satisfying Σ_i n_i[L_i:Q]=2g, R_(L,n)=∏_i M_(n_i)(O_(L_i)) with conjugate-transpose involution.
items.note: API: Define the product ring, adjoint and positive symmetric unit locus; expose factorwise congruence orbits. Tests: (1) one imaginary quadratic factor has n=g; (2) different factors retain separate ranks; (3) this ring need not be realized by a principally polarized variety. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Positive-unit model orbit count
items.statement: n_(L,n) is the number of R_(L,n)^×-orbits on positive self-adjoint units by a↦g*ag.
items.note: API: Construct orbit finiteness, products and log-count only after positivity; separate unweighted counts from masses. Tests: (1) identity is a positive unit; (2) a singular positive-semidefinite matrix is excluded; (3) the action is congruence rather than ordinary conjugation. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Conjectural comparison with the model ring
items.statement: CONJECTURE: for fixed p, A/F_p principally polarizable with simple rational endomorphism fields L_i CM and multiplicities n_i satisfies |log n_A−log n_(L,n)|≤C_p g², uniformly in A and g.
items.note: Explicit proposition-valued hypothesis; never register it as a proved theorem. It excludes the real Frobenius field Q(√p) case and is not repaired by enlarging an O-constant. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Totally positive unit norm labels
items.statement: Σ=O_K^(×,+)/N_(L/K)(O_L^×), with chosen representatives ε_σ; on L^n set h_σ(z,w)=ε_σ z₁ conjugate(w₁)+Σ_(i>1) z_i conjugate(w_i).
items.note: API: Construct the quotient, representative independence, determinants and positive definite hermitian spaces. Tests: (1) the identity label uses ε=1; (2) different unit labels may become equal modulo field norms; (3) n=1 keeps the determinant label visible. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Unitary group of a definite hermitian space
items.statement: U_σ is the K-algebraic group preserving h_σ; its K-points act on O_L-lattices by isometries.
items.note: API: Import affine-group and hermitian-form carriers; build functor of points, localizations and determinant map to the norm-one torus. Tests: (1) the center is anisotropic; (2) unitary is not unitary-similitude; (3) at split finite places the group becomes GL_n. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Integral projective hermitian lattice
items.statement: An O_L-lattice M in L^n is finitely generated, full and locally free of rank n, and integral when h(M,M)⊂O_L. Free lattices form a distinguished subclass.
items.note: API: Use projective modules and localization; prove basis/Gram equivalence only for free modules and retain the Steinitz class. Tests: (1) a nonprincipal ideal gives a rank-one projective module; (2) fullness excludes the zero submodule for n>0; (3) integrality is a pairing condition, not freeness.

items.name: Dual and unimodularity
items.statement: M∨={x∈L^n:h(x,M)⊂O_L}; an integral hermitian lattice is unimodular if M=M∨.
items.note: API: Construct the dual, double dual and localization, and prove determinant-unit criterion when a basis exists. Tests: (1) O_L^n with the standard form is unimodular; (2) integral does not imply self-dual; (3) local self-duality does not imply global freeness.

items.name: Free unimodular lattices and Gram congruence
items.statement: Positive hermitian matrices in GL_n(O_L) modulo congruence correspond to free unimodular hermitian lattices up to isometry, with their determinant unit class retained.
items.note: The realization inside the fixed spaces h_σ additionally uses local classification and the hermitian Hasse principle. The determinant-class condition in (35) is necessary: the same rational space can represent multiple integral unit-norm labels. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Norm ideal of a local hermitian lattice
items.statement: n(M) is the O_(L_v)-ideal generated by h(m,m), m∈M, for a lattice in a fixed localized hermitian space.
items.note: API: Prove isometry invariance, relation to scale ideal and localization; retain dyadic parity. Tests: (1) isometric lattices have equal norm ideals; (2) unimodular dyadic lattices may have different norm ideals; (3) norm and determinant are separate invariants. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Local unimodular classification input
items.statement: In the fixed hermitian space over a local quadratic extension, unimodular lattices of the specified determinant and equal norm ideal are isometric; the norm-ideal restriction is automatic for unramified extensions and for ramified odd residue characteristic.
items.note: G8: Jacobowitz Theorems 7.1,8.2 and Proposition 10.4 must be read for exact dyadic and split conventions. Do not turn the automatic odd-prime case into an all-prime assertion.

items.name: Genus of a hermitian lattice
items.statement: The genus of M comprises projective unimodular lattices in its rational hermitian space locally isometric to M at every finite place, modulo global isometry.
items.note: API: Define local isometry and global classes; prove the adelic double-coset description and isolate free classes. Tests: (1) one genus can have several global classes; (2) class number one for O_L makes projective lattices free; (3) fixing the genus does not fix an integral basis.

items.name: Hermitian genus as a unitary class set
items.statement: For a representative lattice M in a fixed genus, its projective isometry classes identify with U(K)\U(A_(K,fin))/Stab(M).
items.note: This counts all projective lattices; it is not a bijection onto free Gram matrices unless the Steinitz obstruction is removed. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Weighted hermitian genus mass
items.statement: mass(C)=Σ_[M]∈C 1/|Aut(M)| for a positive definite hermitian genus with finitely many isometry classes.
items.note: API: Prove finiteness of automorphism groups and genus, define the weighted sum, and compare it with unweighted cardinality. Tests: (1) one class with two automorphisms has mass 1/2; (2) all automorphisms preserve the hermitian form; (3) mass includes projective nonfree lattices.

items.name: Unitary Tamagawa mass formula
items.statement: For a definite unitary group U of a nondegenerate hermitian space over a CM extension L/K, the genus mass is τ(U)/vol_Tam(K_M), with archimedean compact factors included in K_M; τ(U)=2.
items.note: GN.3 owns this formula and all measure normalizations. Gan–Yu original proof remains G8; the formula alone does not justify the simplified dyadic factors in (39).

items.name: Stabilizer volume of a self-dual hermitian lattice (Gan–Yu), as used in (39)
items.statement: Equation (39) writes the inverse stabilizer volume as a discriminant factor times ∏_(d=1)^n ((d−1)!/(2π)^d)^[K:Q] divided by finite local factors β_(M_v), identified with normalized unitary or orthogonal group orders.
items.note: Recorded as printed and routed to GN.3, which owns local densities and mass formulas: the design job must check it against Gan–Yu Theorem 10.20 and §10.9 (dyadic and ramified places, the choice of orthogonal group at ramified places, split places) before relying on the displayed product. Only its factorial term enters the leading asymptotic. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G4: unacquired Gan–Yu Theorem 10.20, ramified dyadic corrections, nonsmooth naive group models and split local cases prevent routing this displayed simplification as an exact theorem.

items.name: Elementary CM relative-discriminant bound
items.statement: If L=Q(π) is generated by a nonreal p-Weil number and K=L⁺, then N_(K/Q)(D_(L/K))≤(4p)^[K:Q].
items.note: disc_(O_K)(1,π)=(π−conjugate π)², whose real absolute values are 4p sin²θ. The printed p sin²θ misses 4; the O_p([K:Q]) logarithmic scale survives. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Factorial product asymptotic
items.statement: As n→∞, Σ_(d=1)^n log((d−1)!)=(1/2)n² log n−(3/4)n²+O(n log n).
items.note: Expand as Σ_(j=1)^(n−1)(n−j)log j and compare monotone sums to integrals. Thus the displayed factorial product has coefficient 1/2, whereas (51) prints coefficient 1. This audit does not decide which formula the final paper uses. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Mass of unimodular hermitian lattices, corrected (51)–(53)
items.statement: For a CM field L with totally real subfield K arising from a p-Weil number, n ≥ 1 and σ ∈ Σ: log Σ_(M∈C_σ) 1/#Aut(M) = (1/2)[K:Q] n² log n + O_p([K:Q]² n²), and log #C_σ satisfies the same estimate. (Printed: leading coefficient [K:Q] instead of (1/2)[K:Q].)
items.note: E13. The printed coefficient contradicts the factorial product that (39) itself displays. The passage from mass to class number uses Lemma 5.8 (finite-integral-group). Routed to GN.3. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G4: inconsistent with the displayed factorial factor in (39). Also (49) cannot follow from upper residue bounds alone. Unrouted; compare final text and Gan–Yu before any 0.99 threshold.

items.name: Finite general linear group cardinality
items.statement: For a field F_q and n≥0, |GL_n(F_q)|=∏_(i=0)^(n−1)(q^n−q^i)=q^(n²)∏_(j=1)^n(1−q^(−j)).
items.note: The pinned formula is the first product; the normalized second form is elementary algebra. Empty products cover n=0.

items.name: Minkowski finite integral group bound
items.statement: The largest order of a finite subgroup of GL_N(Z) is exp(N log N+O(N)) as N→∞.
items.note: Upper bound: inject at odd congruence primes, choose primes in primitive residue classes, sum valuations and use Σ_(p≤N)log p/p=log N+O(1). Signed permutation matrices give 2^N N! as the matching scale. The congruence and prime estimates remain supplier proof tasks. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Passing from mass to class count
items.statement: For a finite nonempty genus C with 1≤|Aut(M)|≤H, mass(C)≤|C|≤H mass(C). For rank n hermitian O_L-lattices, H≤exp(N log N+O(N)), N=n[L:Q].
items.note: Forget the O_L-structure to embed the finite isometry group in GL_N(Z). A bound on mass alone is not an upper bound for the unweighted count. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Free versus projective mass classes
items.statement: Free unimodular isometry classes form a subset of all projective classes. If Cl(O_L)=1, every finitely generated projective O_L-module of fixed rank is free, so the subset is all classes.
items.note: Retain determinant labels in the union of genera. Class number one is sufficient, not claimed necessary. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Orbit count on a model ring, corrected (55)
items.statement: For a model ring R_(L,n) = ∏_i End_(n_i)(O_(L_i)) with Σ_i [K_i:Q]n_i = g, the number n_(L,n) of ∗-conjugation orbits of R_(L,n)^× on its positive symmetric units satisfies log n_(L,n) ≤ (1/2)Σ_i [K_i:Q] n_i² log n_i + O_p(g²), with equality up to O_p(g²) when every Cl(O_(L_i)) is trivial. (Printed: leading coefficient 1, and "n_(L,n) ≤" for "log n_(L,n) ≤".)
items.note: Corrected by E13: the factorial product in (39) contributes (1/2)[K:Q]n² log n (item factorial-asymptotic). The O_p(g²) error uses Σ[K_i:Q]²n_i² ≤ g² and the p-Weil discriminant bounds; its two-sidedness also needs the residue-ratio lower bound of E12. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G4: the displayed line calls the count itself bounded by this logarithmic quantity, but context requires log count. Its leading coefficient inherits the (39)/(51) discrepancy. Unrouted.

items.name: Convex mass-concentration inequality
items.statement: For g≥0, 1/2<ε<1 and finitely many nonnegative x_i≤εg with Σx_i=g, Σx_i²≤(ε²+(1−ε)²)g².
items.note: Move weight between two interior coordinates until at most one is interior; the maximum has entries εg,(1−ε)g,0,… . This avoids the source interval typo [0,ε]^k and does not depend on the mass formula. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Proposition 5.10, corrected threshold
items.statement: There is g_0, depending on p through the implied constants of (55), such that for g ≥ g_0 and every model ring R_(L,n) with Σ_i [K_i:Q]n_i = g: if log n_(L,n) ≥ 0.495 g² log g then some i_0 has [K_(i_0):Q] = 1 and n_(i_0) ≥ 0.99g. (Printed: threshold 0.99 g² log g, for every g.)
items.note: With the corrected (55), log n_(L,n) ≤ (1/2)Σ[K_i:Q]n_i² log n_i + O_p(g²). If every x_i = [K_i:Q]n_i < 0.99g, Lemma 5.9 gives at most (1/2)(0.9802)g² log g + O(g²); if x_(i_0) ≥ 0.99g with [K_(i_0):Q] ≥ 2, the total is at most 0.255 g² log g + O(g²). Both are below 0.495 g² log g for large g. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.5. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G4: at minimum this is an eventual-in-g statement after controlling uniform O_p(g²) errors, not an all-g implication. The correct threshold also requires the reconciled leading coefficient. Unrouted.

items.name: Density of primes splitting in a class-number-one CM field
items.statement: The nine imaginary quadratic fields of class number one have independent square classes; outside their finite ramified-prime set, the primes splitting in at least one have natural density 1−2^(−9).
items.note: Independent characters and prime equidistribution supply this statement. G8: acquire the class-number-one classification and exact equidistribution proof before closure; the density does not assert a pointwise condition at ramified primes. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Elliptic curve with class-number-one endomorphisms
items.statement: If a prime p splits in an imaginary quadratic class-number-one field L, there exists E/F_p with End_Fp(E)=O_L, obtained from a norm-p algebraic integer and Waterhouse order realization.
items.note: Keep the degree-two Weil polynomial, ordinary reduction and endomorphism-order certificate. This existence statement does not itself determine the mass asymptotic. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Lemma 5.11, corrected: principal polarizations on E^g
items.statement: Let p be a prime that splits in K = Q(√−d) for one of the nine imaginary quadratic fields of class number one (these primes have density 1−2^(−9)). Then there is an elliptic curve E/F_p with End(E) = O_K, and the number of isomorphism classes of principal polarizations on E^g is exp((1/2)g² log g + O_p(g²)). (Printed: exp(g² log g + O(g²)).)
items.note: E13: the leading coefficient is 1/2, from the corrected (55) with [K:Q] = 1 and Cl(O_K) = 1. Every consumer (Theorems 0.2, 0.3, Corollaries 5.13, 5.20) only needs a positive multiple of g² log g, and the thresholds scale. Routed to the finite-field Part II with split-prime-density and cm-elliptic-existence. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G4: the coefficient is withheld with (51). A positive multiple of g² log g would suffice for Theorem 0.3, but the exact leading coefficient is not repaired here. Unrouted.

items.name: Normalized eigenangle spacing measure
items.statement: For a degree-2g Frobenius polynomial, order its 2g eigenangles on the circle with multiplicity, include the wraparound gap, scale gaps by 2g/(2π), and give each gap mass 1/(2g). Average over uniform ppav classes to obtain μ_g.
items.note: API: Define cyclic gaps, tie multiplicities and averaged measures; prove total mass one and permutation invariance. Tests: (1) 2g equal angles give 2g−1 zero gaps; (2) wraparound contributes a gap; (3) repeated eigenvalues must not be deduplicated. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Corollary 5.14, corrected: spacing discrepancy
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of the corrected Theorem 0.2 (main-elliptic-source), let μ_g be the average over g-dimensional ppavs over F_p of their normalized eigenangle spacing measures. Then μ_g({0}) ≥ 0.99 − o(1), so the Kolmogorov distance between μ_g and the atomless GUE spacing law satisfies liminf_(g→∞) discrep(μ_g, μ_GUE) ≥ 0.99.
items.note: E15: h equal roots give h−1 zero gaps, so a factor E^h or B0^(h/2) forces zero-gap mass at least (h−1)/g, not h/g; the loss is o(1). The metric is not specified in the paper; the Kolmogorov distance is the one for which the argument works. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.5. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G5/G7: should specify an asymptotic lower bound, the exact discrepancy metric and normalized spacing law. Two eigenvalues each of multiplicity h force at least 2(h−1) zero gaps, so finite-g mass is at least h/g−1/g, not h/g. Unrouted.

items.name: Cohen–Lenstra probability measure
items.statement: For a prime ℓ, CL_ℓ assigns a finite abelian ℓ-group H mass c_ℓ/|Aut(H)|, c_ℓ=∏_(j≥1)(1−ℓ^(−j)); for finite S use the product of these measures.
items.note: API: Construct the countable isomorphism-class space, positive normalization and finite-prime product; keep it separate from symplectic Frobenius models. Tests: (1) trivial group has mass c_ℓ; (2) the prime set S is finite; (3) being a heuristic for a family requires a separate hypothesis.

items.name: Random integral matrices and Cohen–Lenstra
items.statement: For Haar-uniform F∈M_g(Z_ℓ), coker(1−F) converges in distribution on finite abelian ℓ-group classes to CL_ℓ as g→∞.
items.note: The matrix is drawn from all endomorphisms, not GL_g. G8: original Friedman–Washington proof and almost-sure finiteness remain to acquire.

items.name: Proposed enhanced Cohen–Lenstra law
items.statement: For distinct positive n₁,…,n_k, the source defines CL_(n,ℓ)(H₁,…,H_k) by the g→∞ limit of Haar probabilities that coker(1−F^(n_j))≅H_j for every j; CL_(n,S) is the finite-prime product.
items.note: G7: Definition 5.16 writes a limit without proving general existence. Route the finite-g construction and existence task, not an assumed limiting measure. API: Treat existence, tightness and total probability one as proof obligations before packaging a probability measure; define the finite-g joint laws first. Tests: (1) repeated exponents are excluded by the source; (2) n=(1) recovers the ordinary model; (3) shared F makes components at different exponents dependent. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Two-extension zero-cokernel probability at two
items.statement: For F uniform in M_g(F₂), P(det(1−F²)≠0)=|GL_g(F₂)|/2^(g²)=∏_(j=1)^g(1−2^(−j)), with positive infinite-product limit.
items.note: 1−F²=(1−F)² in characteristic two; translation F↦1−F is a bijection on all matrices. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Uniform positive bound at odd primes
items.statement: For odd ℓ and F uniform in M_g(F_ℓ), P(det(1−F²)≠0)≥2∏_(j≥1)(1−3^(−j))−1>0.
items.note: Union bound excludes eigenvalues ±1. This lower bound proves a positive liminf; it alone does not prove convergence of the joint law. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Source enhanced-statistics conjecture
items.statement: CONJECTURE: when CL_S models the S-primary point groups of a geometric family over F_p and p∉S, the enhanced law CL_(n,S) models the joint S-primary point groups over F_(p^(n_j)).
items.note: Explicit speculative implication, conditioned on existence of the enhanced law and a specified convergence meaning. No blanket theorem about geometric families is asserted. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Lemma 5.19, corrected: odd characteristic
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime and E/F_p an elliptic curve. Then E(F_p) and E(F_(p²)) are not both p-groups. For p = 2 the statement is false exactly for the curves with trace a = ±1, for example y²+xy = x³+x²+1 (a = 1), with #E(F_2) = 2 and #E(F_4) = 8.
items.note: Proof: put #E(F_p) = p+1−a and #E(F_(p²)) = (p+1−a)(p+1+a). If both are p-powers, p^i + p^j = 2p+2 with p^i = p+1−a and p^j = p+1+a. For odd p, reduction mod p forces i = 0 or j = 0, and then p^(j) = 2p+1 (or p^(i) = 2p+1), which has no solution. For p = 2, {i,j} = {1,2}, that is a = ±1. This replaces the p ≥ 7 repair of the earlier checkpoints (whose argument is kept in the history) and the withheld literal item elliptic-pgroups-source. The printed proof (a = b = 1, then det = 0) is wrong for every p: see E17. [cc-442dc5]

items.name: Point counts are isogeny invariant
items.statement: For A/F_q, #A(F_(q^r))=det(1−Frob_q^r|V_ℓA), so point counts are invariant under F_q-isogeny and multiply on products.
items.note: An isogeny need not identify rational point groups; only their orders are used in the large-factor argument. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Corollary 5.20, corrected: odd p
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime satisfying the corrected conclusion of Lemma 5.11, assume the hypotheses of the corrected Theorem 0.2, and assume the limits defining CL_((1,2),v) exist (E16). Let S be the set of primes below p²+2p+1 other than p. Then with probability tending to 1 a random g-dimensional ppav A over F_p has A(F_p)_S ≠ 0 or A(F_(p²))_S ≠ 0, whereas CL_((1,2),S)(0,0) > 0; so the enhanced Cohen–Lenstra model (Conjecture 5.18) does not describe the joint distribution of (A(F_p)_S, A(F_(p²))_S) for random ppavs.
items.note: Lemma 5.19 holds for odd p (elliptic-pgroups-large), and a factor B0 contributes #B0(F_p) = (p−1)², whose prime factors lie in S when p is odd. For p = 2 the argument fails twice: curves with trace ±1 over F_2 have 2-group point groups over F_2 and F_4, and #B0(F_2) = #B0(F_4) = 1 (E17). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.5. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G5/G6/G7: the stated proof invokes the false p=2 lemma, unclosed concentration and an unspecified limiting law. The zero-cokernel event comparison can be repaired only after those hypotheses are resolved. Unrouted.

items.name: Remark 4.8, corrected: trace versus reduced trace
items.statement: Let A be a simple g-dimensional abelian variety, D = End⁰(A), Z its centre, e = [Z:Q] and [D:Z] = m². Then em divides 2g and t = (2g/(em))·Trd_(D/Q) on D. (Printed: t = Trd_(D/Q), which holds only when em = 2g, for example when D is a CM field of degree 2g.)
items.note: E10. The characteristic polynomial of h ∈ D on V_ℓ(A) is the (2g/(em))-th power of its reduced characteristic polynomial over Q (Mumford §19, Theorem 4 and §21). Routed to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6 with endomorphism-trace. [cc-442dc5] Earlier note: G3: false without a multiplicity factor in general. If End⁰(A)=Q and dim A=g>0, t(1)=2g but reduced trace_Q/Q(1)=1. The checked Conrad trace definition keeps the actual Tate representation. Unrouted literal claim.

items.name: Ramified-prime count from the relative discriminant
items.statement: For L/K generated by a p-Weil number with d=[K:Q], the number of finite primes of K ramifying in L is at most d log(4p)/log 2.
items.note: Every ramified prime divides the relative discriminant and has norm at least 2; multiply their norms and use relative-discriminant. This avoids the extra factor d in the source estimate. Ownership checked against the 211 atlas records, relevant full descriptions and reviewed audits at the recorded explorer commit; no matching pinned implementation found beyond the explicit library imports.

items.name: Monogenic trace-dual formula
items.statement: For an integrally closed domain A with fraction field K, a finite separable field extension L/K and integral x generating L/K, the trace-form dual of A[x] is (minpoly_K(x)'(x))⁻¹·A[x].
items.note: Actual statement and proof read, including standing hypotheses. The source order need not be integrally closed: A, not A[x], carries that hypothesis. Use the existing trace dual, not a new LT-specific carrier.

items.name: Hensel lifting from adic completeness
items.statement: An I-adically complete ring is Henselian at I. A monic polynomial with an approximate root modulo I and invertible derivative in the quotient has a congruent exact root.
items.note: The declarations were read in full. These are generic imports; finite-order completeness, its local residue field, the unramified coefficient DVR and continuous power-series evaluation are still adapters.

items.name: Length under restriction of local scalars
items.statement: For a local algebra map A→B and compatible B-module M, length_A(M)=length_B(M)·length_(ResidueField A)(ResidueField B), with the library's extended-natural length conventions.
items.note: Actual statement/proof and hypotheses read. Apply to the unramified coefficient DVR over Z_ℓ; prove the finite-length and residue-degree identifications before converting to natural exponents.

items.name: Monogenic conductor and dual sandwich
items.statement: Let O=Z_ℓ, K=Q_ℓ, F=K(θ), f=minpoly_K θ monic integral irreducible, R=O[θ], S=O_F, β=f'(θ), δ=v_ℓ disc(f). Then βS⊆R and #S/βS=ℓ^δ. If R⊆M⊆S is a full R-lattice, N=βM^∨ is an R-ideal in R and length_O(R/N)=length_O(M/R)≤δ; dual homothety classes, not identical classes, are represented by N.
items.note: Import ordinary field-trace duality, integrality of traces, finite-DVR determinant/index and discriminant=±Norm(β). Use the trace-dual involution for the rank-one class count; do not identify N with the original class of M.
items.proof: See continuation L1–L9 in the adjacent report; mathematical proof plan, not a Lean proof.

items.name: Residue-correct coefficient DVR
items.statement: For the local monogenic order R above, write R/rad R=F_(ℓ^s). There is an unramified coefficient DVR O₀⊂R with that residue field and t∈rad R such that R=O₀[t] and O₀[[T]]→R, T↦t, is surjective. Every finite R-quotient has Z_ℓ-length s times its O₀-length.
items.note: Lift the residue of θ via a monic lift of its separable irreducible polynomial; put t=θ−w. Complete finite local algebra, topological evaluation and residue-cardinality identifications remain explicit adapters. No quotient of Z_ℓ[[T]] is asserted when s>1.
items.proof: See continuation L1–L9 in the adjacent report; mathematical proof plan, not a Lean proof.

items.name: Weighted partition cumulative bound
items.statement: For a complete DVR with residue cardinality Q≥2 let H_Q(j)=Σ_(λ⊢j)Q^(j−length λ). Then H_Q(0)=1, H_Q(j)≤(Q+1)^(j−1) for j≥1 and Σ_(j=0)^a H_Q(j)≤(Q+1)^a≤Q^(2a). Consequently R has at most ℓ^(2δ) ideals of Z_ℓ-colength ≤δ.
items.note: Inject partitions into ordered compositions, sum their weights with the binomial theorem, then take a=floor(δ/s). Retain j=0 and δ=0; this avoids the false weak-composition estimate in LT (13).
items.proof: See continuation L1–L9 in the adjacent report; mathematical proof plan, not a Lean proof.

items.name: Rank-one local ideal-class bound
items.statement: Under the local-order hypotheses, the number C₁ of F×-orbits of full R-lattices in F is at most ℓ^(2δ). A finite covering list is given by the trace duals of the ideals in R of colength at most δ.
items.note: Normalize SM=S, divide M by one of its S-unit elements to obtain R⊆M⊆S, and apply βM^∨. Duality induces a bijection of homothety classes. The selected list is dualized; no unjustified direct representative choice.
items.proof: See continuation L1–L9 in the adjacent report; mathematical proof plan, not a Lean proof.

items.name: Repeated-block local orbit bound
items.statement: Let C_n be the number of GL_n(F)-orbits on full R-lattices in F^n, n≥1. Then C_n≤C_(n−1)C₁ℓ^((n−1)δ), hence C_n≤ℓ^((n(n−1)/2+2n)δ)≤ℓ^(2n²δ). When δ=0 the bound is one.
items.note: Induct using a fixed F-coordinate flag. Normalize prefix and quotient by block-diagonal centralizers, then divide graph fibers by rational commuting shears. Count parabolic orbits first, which surject onto full centralizer orbits. This quadratic-in-n replacement does not certify the source's linear exponent 4nδ. It replaces the withheld literal item local-orbit-source (v1 (13): ℓ^(4nδ)); the printed count and its failing step are E1, and (14)'s exponent is E19. [cc-442dc5]
items.proof: See continuation L1–L9 in the adjacent report; mathematical proof plan, not a Lean proof.

items.name: Semisimple local orbit bound with multiplicities
items.statement: For an integral semisimple γ with characteristic polynomial ∏f_i^n_i, define δ_i=v_ℓ disc(f_i), ρ_ij=v_ℓ Res(f_i,f_j), Δ=Σn_i²δ_i+2Σ_(i<j)n_i n_jρ_ij. Its full-centralizer lattice-orbit count is at most ℓ^(Σ_i[n_i(n_i−1)/2+2n_i]δ_i+Σ_(i<j)n_i n_jρ_ij)≤ℓ^(2Δ).
items.locator: LT §§3.1.1–3.1.6 and Yun Lemma 4.9; continuation L7
items.note: The disjoint-spectrum Sylvester operator is invertible, so its determinant contributes each unordered pair once with multiplicity n_i n_j. This reproves the flag-fiber extension with repeated blocks; it does not cite Yun's regular-semisimple theorem beyond its hypotheses.
items.proof: See continuation L1–L9 in the adjacent report; mathematical proof plan, not a Lean proof.

items.name: Adelic local-orbit bound for Weil polynomials
items.statement: Let a monic integral characteristic polynomial of degree m have complex roots of absolute value √p and semisimple local realizations. The product of local centralizer lattice-orbit counts is at most D_*²≤(2√p)^(2m(m−1)), where D_* is the absolute product of differences of ordered unequal root occurrences, with multiplicities. For m=2g the last exponent is 4g(2g−1).
items.note: D_* is a nonzero Galois-invariant algebraic integer, hence an integer, and its ℓ-valuation is Δ_ℓ. Almost all local factors are one. This counts only restricted-product local orbits, not rational adelic class sets or global abelian varieties; the general stabilizer bound is still missing. F,V reduction uses the existing prime-field adapter, not a nonprime-field semilinear claim. With multiplicities, D_*² ≤ (2√p)^(4g(2g−1)) is the corrected form of v1 (14), matching Lee 2022 §3.1(1)(c); see E19. [cc-442dc5]
items.proof: See continuation L1–L9 in the adjacent report; mathematical proof plan, not a Lean proof.

items.name: Isotypic integral stabilizer via a congruence kernel
items.statement: If R^n⊆M⊆S^n, β=f'(θ), then ker(GL_n(S)→GL_n(S/βS))⊆Stab(M). Consequently [GL_n(S):Stab(M)]≤ℓ^(n²δ). This includes δ=0, when the stabilizer is all GL_n(S).
items.note: For g in the kernel, (g−1)M⊆βS^n⊆M; apply the same to g⁻¹ for equality. Bound the finite image by all n×n matrices. The normalization SM=S^n puts Stab(M) inside GL_n(S). This proves only the isotypic bound and does not close the general nonisotypic global exponent in (20).
items.proof: See continuation L1–L9 in the adjacent report; mathematical proof plan, not a Lean proof.

items.name: Full-rank PID quotient in Smith coordinates
items.statement: For a domain R that is a principal ideal ring, a finite basis b of an R-module M and N≤M with equal R-finrank, there is an R-linear equivalence (M/N) ≃ ∏ᵢ R/(aᵢ), with aᵢ the nonzero Smith coefficients of the inclusion N→M.
items.note: Freshly read at the pinned Mathlib commit. This is PID-generic; do not substitute the Z-only quotientEquivPiZMod or natAbs_det_basis_change.

items.name: Cardinality of a prime-power quotient
items.statement: In a Dedekind domain S, for a nonzero prime ideal P and i∈ℕ, cardQuot(P^i)=cardQuot(P)^i. Here cardQuot is Nat.card of the quotient, so explicit finite residue field hypotheses are supplied before interpreting this as a finite positive count.
items.note: The first declaration is in the root namespace, not Ideal. Freshly read its prime-ideal context and induction through successive quotients. For a DVR with finite residue field, the displayed positive cardinal also excludes an infinite quotient.

items.name: Unit times uniformizer power in a DVR
items.statement: For a nonzero element x in a discrete valuation ring R and an irreducible uniformizer π, there are n∈ℕ and u∈R× with x=uπ^n.
items.note: Freshly read at the pinned commit. Combined with Smith coordinates, this identifies principal-ideal quotients with powers of the maximal ideal; normalized valuations of units are zero.

items.name: Representative criterion for a double coset
