items.statement: For any group G, subgroups H,K≤G and a,b∈G, DoubleCoset.mk H K a = DoubleCoset.mk H K b iff there are h∈H and k∈K with b=hak.
items.note: Read the whole pinned file. The actual carrier is DoubleCoset.Quotient, with capital Q. This does not itself construct a nested-level map or assert a fiber size.

items.name: Index of a stabilizer equals its orbit cardinal
items.statement: For any group G acting on X and x∈X, (MulAction.stabilizer G x).index=(MulAction.orbit G x).ncard.
items.note: No finiteness of G is assumed. The local argument first proves the orbit finite; otherwise the Nat-valued index/cardinality can be zero for an infinite orbit. Do not apply finite-group cardinal division to an infinite compact group.

items.name: Determinant index of a stable DVR lattice
items.statement: Let O be a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field of size q, fraction field K and normalized additive valuation v. Let T be a finite free O-lattice spanning a finite-dimensional K-space W. If F∈GL_K(W) and F(T)⊆T, then T/F(T) and F⁻¹(T)/T are finite of cardinality q^{v(det_K F)}, and F induces an O-linear equivalence F⁻¹(T)/T ≃ T/F(T). This includes rank zero and v(det F)=0.
items.locator: Yun v2 Lemma 4.9 determinant/length step; continuation S1
items.note: A missing assembly adapter on existing Submodule/LinearMap quotients, not a new DVR or lattice carrier. Finite residue cardinality and invertibility are load-bearing.
items.proof: S1: apply Smith normal form to F(T)≤T; write each nonzero diagonal coefficient as u_iπ^{a_i}; multiply q^{a_i}; det(F) differs from their product by a unit because a domain basis maps to a basis of F(T). The displayed map sends x+T to F(x)+F(T), with inverse F⁻¹.
tests: Unit determinant gives one class.
A diagonal map diag(π,π²) gives q³ classes, not q².
Without invertibility, the zero map on rank one has infinite cokernel and is excluded.

items.name: Integral stabilizer controlled by successive graded lattices
items.statement: Let ℓ be prime, O=Z_ℓ and K=Q_ℓ. Let γ be integral semisimple with characteristic polynomial ∏_{i=1}^r f_i^{n_i}, where the distinct f_i∈O[X] are monic irreducible and n_i≥1. Put F_i=K[X]/f_i, R_i=O[θ_i], S_i=O_{F_i}, V=⊕F_i^{n_i}, δ_i=v_ℓ disc(f_i), ρ_ij=v_ℓ Res(f_i,f_j), and Δ=Σn_i²δ_i+2Σ_{i<j}n_i n_jρ_ij. For every full γ-stable lattice M there is a conjugate H_M of ∏GL_{n_i}(S_i) containing Stab_{Z_γ(K)}(M), with [H_M:Stab(M)]≤ℓ^{Σn_i²δ_i+Σ_{i<j}n_i n_jρ_ij}≤ℓ^Δ.
items.locator: LT v1 §§3.1.1,3.2.1, especially (20); Yun v2 Lemma 4.9 proof; replacement proof S2–S3
items.note: This is a proposed replacement proof, not the printed argument. H_M is built from the saturations of successive quotients pr_i(M∩V_{≤i}); these are not M∩V_i and are not replaced by the saturation of M itself. It replaces the withheld literal item stabilizer-depth-source (v1 (16)–(20)); the printed map is E2 and (20)'s exponent E19. [cc-442dc5]
items.proof: S2–S3: normalize each successive quotient U_i so R_i^{n_i}⊆U_i⊆S_i^{n_i}. Any stabilizer preserves U_i and S_iU_i, hence lies in H. The H-orbit maps equivariantly to ∏H_i·U_i, whose size is at most ℓ^{Σn_i²δ_i}. Each fixed-profile fiber has exactly ℓ^{Σ_{i<j}n_i n_jρ_ij} raw stable lattices: induct using graph classes killed by the invertible Sylvester operator on Hom_K(V_i,V_{<i}) modulo Hom_O(U_i,L_{<i}). Multiply the two bounds, use index_stabilizer, then conjugate back.
tests: One isotypic block recovers L9.
All discriminants and cross resultants units force index one.
Multiplicities (2,1) contribute 2ρ to the fiber exponent, not ρ or 4ρ.
For λ=(0,2,4) over Q₂ the rank-one graded profile has 2⁴=16 lattices, with the middle quotient an image, not an intersection.

items.name: Nested right-level map on double cosets
items.statement: For any group G, H≤G and K'≤K≤G, construct π:DoubleCoset.Quotient H K'→DoubleCoset.Quotient H K by π([g])=[g]. For each g define a surjection of sets K/K'→π⁻¹([g]), kK'↦[gk], using left cosets kK' of the subgroup K' inside K; neither subgroup is required normal.
items.locator: LT v1 §3.2, (15) and use of (20); AA.4 level-map specialization; continuation S4
items.note: Reuse DoubleCoset.Quotient and the subgroup-of carrier for K' inside K. These quotients are sets, not quotient groups; retain H∩gKg⁻¹ stabilizers. Proposed home: TauCeti/NumberTheory/AdelicAlgebraicGroups/LevelMaps/DoubleCoset.lean. Reuse Mathlib's quotient API; no private replacement or upstream contribution is required.
api: π_mk: π(mk H K' g)=mk H K g.
fiber_surjection_respects_cosets: k₂=k₁s with s∈K' gives the same fine double coset; no normality.
tests: K'=K gives the identity map and singleton fibers.
H=1 gives exactly [K:K'] fine classes per coarse class when the index is finite.
H=G gives one fine class, even if [K:K']>1; equality with the level index is false.
Take nonnormal K' generated by a transposition in S₃ and K=S₃: construction is still well-defined.
items.proof: S4: DoubleCoset.eq shows well-definedness of π. For a class in the fiber choose x=h g k using that same criterion, then [x]=[gk] at the finer level. Coset representatives k differing on the right by K' give the same fine class.

items.name: Finite-index bound for a double-coset level change
items.statement: For a group G and subgroups H,K',K with K'≤K and finite index N=[K:K'], every fiber of H\G/K'→H\G/K has at most N elements. If H\G/K is finite of cardinal h, then H\G/K' is finite of cardinal at most Nh. No freeness, normality, neatness or finite-group assumption is made.
items.locator: LT v1 §3.2.3 level-index step; continuation S4
items.note: A bound for coarse sets only, not a claim of an unramified degree-N covering or a quotient-group structure.
items.proof: Use the surjection from the finite set K/K' onto each fiber. With a finite base, the fine quotient is equivalent as a set to the finite dependent sum of its fibers; sum their cardinalities.
tests: H=G and nontrivial N gives strict inequality 1<N.
H=1 attains equality.
N=1 makes the level map bijective.

items.name: Conjugate right levels have equivalent double-coset sets
items.statement: For a group G, H,K≤G and a∈G, put K_a=aKa⁻¹. Then H\G/K_a ≃ H\G/K via [g]↦[ga], with inverse [x]↦[xa⁻¹]. The conjugating element need not lie in H or normalize H.
items.locator: LT v1 §3.2 choice of integral compact subgroup; continuation S5
items.note: Right multiplication, not conjugation of representatives. This is what permits orbit-dependent compact levels without assuming a rational conjugating element.
items.proof: If g'=h g(a k a⁻¹), then g'a=h(ga)k. Apply the inverse formula and quotient induction for the two identity laws.
tests: a=1 is the identity.
With H a transposition subgroup in S₃ and a outside its normalizer, the equivalence still holds.
Changing [g] to [a⁻¹ga] would change the left subgroup and is not this map.

items.name: Index of product subgroups with finite exceptional support
items.statement: For groups H_v and subgroups S_v≤H_v, suppose S_v=H_v outside a finite set B and [H_v:S_v] is finite for every v∈B. Then (∏H_v)/(∏S_v) is equivalent as a set to ∏_{v∈B}(H_v/S_v), and [∏H_v:∏S_v]=∏_{v∈B}[H_v:S_v]. In a restricted-product ambient group, this applies to the everywhere-compact product and its componentwise stabilizer when those products are subgroups of the specified ambient group.
items.locator: LT v1 (20), local-to-global index step; continuation S5
items.note: No infinite cardinal multiplication, normality or Haar measure is needed. Finite exceptional support is an explicit input, not a conclusion of the abstract theorem.
items.proof: S5: map a coset to its component cosets. Equality is exactly coordinatewise subgroup membership. Lift the finitely many representatives and fill the remaining coordinates with identity; this gives the inverse on cosets.
tests: Empty B gives index one.
Two factors of indices 2 and 3 give index 6.
Infinitely many proper finite-index factors are excluded; their product quotient can be infinite.

items.name: Conditional rational-orbit bound from local lattices
items.statement: Let a group G_f with subgroup Γ act on a lattice space X, with at most D_*² G_f-orbits. Suppose h=#(Γ\G_f/K₀)<∞ for a fixed compact level K₀. For every orbit representative M assume Stab(M)=∏S_{M,ℓ}, contained in K_M=∏H_{M,ℓ}=a_M K₀ a_M⁻¹ with a_M∈G_f, equality S_{M,ℓ}=H_{M,ℓ} away from finitely many primes, and ∏[H_{M,ℓ}:S_{M,ℓ}]≤D_*. Then Γ\X is finite and #Γ\X≤D_*³h. In the semisimple Weil-lattice setting of L8 and S3, where these group-identification and finite-support inputs are established, D_*≤(2√p)^{m(m−1)} gives #Γ\X≤(2√p)^{3m(m−1)}h.
items.note: Explicitly conditional on the global action, product stabilizers, restricted-product conjugacy and coarse class-set finiteness. No class-number estimate, Tate/Honda/Waterhouse classification, quaternionic norm comparison, nonprime-field extension or sharp numerical coefficient is proved here.
items.proof: Decompose X into G_f-orbits, identify the Γ-orbits in G_f·M with Γ\G_f/Stab(M), bound each by D_* times #Γ\G_f/K_M, transport the latter by [g]↦[ga_M] to the fixed class set of size h, and sum over at most D_*² orbits.
tests: D_*=1 leaves at most h rational orbits, not necessarily one.
With Γ=G_f each transitive orbit contributes one, so the upper bound need not be sharp.
Removing the finite-support or conjugacy hypotheses does not permit this conclusion.

items.name: Finite semisimple-module bicommutant supplier
items.statement: For a semisimple R-module M finite as a module over End_R(M), the canonical action R→End_{End_R(M)}(M) is surjective. Faithfulness is required to upgrade this surjection to an isomorphism onto the bicommutant.
items.note: Read the complete statements and their ambient IsSemisimpleModule hypothesis. This is already the semisimple, not merely simple, density theorem. Tate’s application still needs the finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-algebra/module hypotheses and the linear centralizer translation.

items.name: Compactness of p-adic integers
items.statement: For a prime ℓ, the topological space Z_ℓ is compact. Finite matrix powers inherit compactness; identifying End_Zℓ(T) with such a power requires a finite free basis and its compatible topology.
items.note: The named instance was read. It supplies compact coefficients, not an already-built Tate module or a topology on its endomorphism ring.

items.name: Convergent subsequences in first-countable compact sets
items.statement: In a first-countable topological space, a sequence contained in a compact set has a strictly increasing subsequence converging to a point of that set.
items.note: Read IsCompact.tendsto_subseq with its FirstCountableTopology hypothesis. The application uses finite-dimensional ℓ-adic matrix spaces; compactness without first countability is not silently substituted.

items.name: Finite-field finiteness at fixed polarization degree
items.statement: For fixed finite field k, dimension g and integer d≥1, only finitely many k-isomorphism classes of abelian varieties B/k of dimension g admit a k-defined polarization of degree d². This does not assert finiteness after forgetting the degree constraint.
items.note: Import finite-type polarized moduli and the rational-family/twist comparison from PELModuli M2/M5/M6. Coarse rational points alone are not a proof about k-isomorphism classes. Tate also gives a bounded projective-embedding route; its Mumford/Weil inputs are not read here. The finiteness is used before, not deduced from, the unpolarized counting endpoint. The finite-field finiteness adapter is not itself a matching baseline declaration or an explicit M6 theorem, so it remains missing while its moduli suppliers are planned. The required finite-type statement includes p dividing d; good-prime smoothness in M2 does not by itself supply it.

items.name: Prime-to-characteristic divisibility of a polarization
items.statement: Let B/k be an abelian variety, ℓ≠char(k), n≥0, and λ:B→B∨ a k-defined polarization. If its Tate alternating pairing takes values in ℓ^n Z_ℓ(1), then λ=ℓ^n μ for a unique k-defined polarization μ. In dimension g, deg μ=ℓ^(−2gn) deg λ.
items.locator: Tate 1966 Proposition 1 proof, p.137, invoking Weil [12]
items.note: A2 owns the positivity and polarization criterion; A3 supplies the perfect torsion pairing and factorization through [ℓ^n]. Divisibility of a scheme homomorphism follows by killing B[ℓ^n]; positivity of the divided symmetric homomorphism is a separate A2 obligation, not a bare matrix assertion. The original Weil proof remains a G8 source leaf.
items.proof: Reduce the integral pairing modulo ℓ^n and use the perfect B[ℓ^n]–B∨[ℓ^n] pairing to show λ kills B[ℓ^n]. Factor through its quotient [ℓ^n], descend the unique factor, and use the positive rational scaling criterion for polarizations. Apply the degree formula for [ℓ^n].
tests: n=0 gives μ=λ.
On an elliptic curve λ=[ℓ^n]λ₀ has degree ℓ^(2n)deg λ₀, not ℓ^n deg λ₀.
The argument does not replace p-primary group schemes by geometric points.

items.name: Tate’s isotropic image lemma
items.statement: Let A/k have a k-polarization θ of degree d², let ℓ≠char(k), and assume Tate’s Hyp(k,A,d,ℓ): only finitely many k-isomorphism classes B admitting a degree-d² k-polarization and an ℓ-power isogeny B→A. Every Galois-stable maximal isotropic Q_ℓ-subspace W⊆V_ℓ(A) for θ is the image of some u∈End_k(A)⊗Q_ℓ.
items.note: C1 of the continuation expands the full proof. The auxiliary isogenies are built from finite étale torsion and A3 quotients; they do not presuppose Tate full faithfulness or the marked-classification endpoint. Hyp is a hypothesis here, supplied over finite fields by fixed-polarization-finiteness.
items.proof: Put T=T_ℓA and X_n=(T∩W)+ℓ^nT; T∩W is saturated of rank g, so [T:X_n]=ℓ^(ng). Quotient by the subgroup represented by ℓ^(−n)X_n/T, then factor [ℓ^n] to obtain f_n:B_n→A with f_nT_ℓB_n=X_n. Divide f_n*θ by ℓ^n using polarization-divisibility; all B_n have a degree-d² polarization. On an infinite subsequence B_i≅B_n, the matrices u_i=f_i v_i f_n^(−1) preserve X_n. Compactness gives u_i→u in the closed finite-dimensional endomorphism algebra. For x∈∩X_i choose preimages y_i∈X_n and a convergent subsequence; continuity gives u(y)=x. Conversely every u(y) lies in every closed X_i. Thus u(X_n)=T∩W and u(V)=W.
tests: For g=0 take u=0.
X_n has index ℓ^(ng) without assuming the chosen polarization is principal.
Limits of images require the compact preimage argument, not an unsupported interchange of image and intersection.

items.name: Tate full faithfulness at a split Frobenius prime
items.statement: For A/F_q, ℓ≠p, suppose Q_ℓ[π] is a product of copies of Q_ℓ. Then End_Fq(A)⊗Q_ℓ equals the commutant of π on V_ℓ(A).
items.locator: Tate 1966 Proposition 2 and following paragraph, pp.137–138
items.note: This is the arithmetic application of existing semisimple bicommutant theory, not a new generic density theorem. The finite-field assumption supplies both Hyp and the Frobenius-generated Galois algebra.
items.proof: Let E_ℓ be the realized endomorphism algebra and D its commutant. Maximal π-stable isotropic subspaces are images of E_ℓ-elements, so D-stable. Descend on dimension: W⊥/W is split semisimple of even dimension at least two, giving two distinct stable line extensions whose intersection is W. Hence every π-eigenline is D-stable. Each d∈D is scalar on every eigenspace, so D=Q_ℓ[π]. Apply the semisimple bicommutant supplier to recover E_ℓ=End_π(V_ℓA).
tests: A repeated eigenvalue is allowed; all lines in its eigenspace force a single scalar action of D there.
The split-prime hypothesis is removed only after the independent characteristic-polynomial dimension argument, not by this lemma alone.
A nonsplit irreducible Frobenius block has no Q_ℓ-eigenline and is not covered by this proof.

items.name: Integral Tate full faithfulness at the characteristic prime
items.statement: For abelian varieties A,B/F_q, let C(A),C(B) be the contravariant Dieudonné modules of their p-divisible groups over W(F_q), with their F,V actions. The natural map Hom_Fq(A,B)⊗Z_p→Hom_{W(F_q),F,V}(C(B),C(A)) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: WM71 Part II Theorem 1, pp.60–61; integral saturation in Part I pp.55–57; Waterhouse 1969 §1.2.
items.note: D1–D4 incorporate handoff P1–P3 and a fresh reading of the original WM71/M68 proofs. Rational full faithfulness and independent characteristic-polynomial comparison are now separate items. Original R07.2 classification and A3/A6 geometric proofs and generic adapter audits remain G8. Status remains missing.
tests: The direction is C(B)→C(A), not C(A)→C(B).
For q=p both F,V are Z_p-linear; for q=p^a with a>1 they remain oppositely semilinear.
Using A[p](k̄) loses the connected p-primary part and cannot give this theorem.
items.proof: Both sides are finite free Z_p-modules. Rational p-Tate gives equal rank. The saturated injection has finite torsion cokernel with no p-torsion, hence zero; it is the required integral isomorphism.

items.name: Prime-field linear-dual realization
items.statement: For A/F_p put D^lin₀(A)=Hom_Zp(C(A),Z_p), where C is Waterhouse’s contravariant module. Set F_D(φ)=φ∘F_C and V_D(φ)=φ∘V_C. For f:A→B define D^lin₀(f)(φ)=φ∘C(f). This is a covariant finite free Z_p-realization of rank 2dim A with F_D V_D=V_D F_D=p and π_D=F_D; rationalize by tensoring with Q_p. This specifies the prime-field convention, not the general-q Cartier-dual convention.
items.locator: Waterhouse 1969 §§1.2 and 2.1; LT v1 Remark 3.2; continuation C3
items.note: Use the existing linear dual and imported R07.2 contravariant equivalence; do not build a second Dieudonné category. At F_p no scalar Frobenius twist is needed. The inherited general-q D₀ remains a separate convention-comparison task. API: see the structured entries below.

api.name: PrimeFieldDieudonne.linearDual
api.statement: Form the Z_p-linear dual of C(A), with transposed F and V.

api.name: PrimeFieldDieudonne.map_apply
api.statement: For f:A→B, φ∈D^lin₀(A), x∈C(B), D^lin₀(f)(φ)(x)=φ(C(f)(x)).

api.name: PrimeFieldDieudonne.map_comp
api.statement: For f:A→B and g:B→C, D^lin₀(g∘f)=D^lin₀(g)∘D^lin₀(f), and identity maps to identity.

api.name: PrimeFieldDieudonne.frobenius
api.statement: The realization of the F_p-Frobenius of A is F_D, and V_D=pF_D^(−1) after rationalization.

api.name: PrimeFieldDieudonne.annihilatorLattice
api.statement: Full superlattices L⊇D^lin₀(A) in its rational space correspond by Z_p-duality to full sublattices L∨⊆C(A), reversing inclusion and preserving simultaneous F,V-stability.

uses.how: Turns a p-primary subgroup quotient into a superlattice in the same covariant transport direction as ℓ≠p.
Identifies rational Frobenius with the linear F operator used in local lattice counting.

tests.name: PrimeFieldDieudonne.zero_rank
tests.statement: The zero abelian variety has zero dual module and singleton full-lattice space.

tests.name: PrimeFieldDieudonne.matrix_transpose
tests.statement: For C=Z_p², F_C=diag(1,p), V_C=diag(p,1), the dual has the same diagonal matrices and F_D V_D=pI; this is transpose, not an F/V swap.

tests.name: PrimeFieldDieudonne.scaling_direction
tests.statement: The isogeny [p] induces pI covariantly; pulling back the target lattice under [p] gives p^(−1)D^lin₀, while the contravariant image is pC.

tests.name: PrimeFieldDieudonne.nonprime_scalar
tests.statement: Over F_(p²), choose w∈W(F_(p²)) with σ(w)≠w. For σ-linear F, φ∘F is σ-semilinear, not W-linear, so the displayed prime-field formula is not a general-q construction.

items.name: Torsion detects integral quasi-homomorphisms
items.statement: For A,B/F_p and α∈Hom(A,B)⊗Q, α is an actual F_p-homomorphism if and only if it maps T_ℓ(A) into T_ℓ(B) for every ℓ≠p and maps D^lin₀(A) into D^lin₀(B) at p. For a rational quasi-isogeny, carrying all these lattices onto their targets is equivalent to being an isomorphism.
items.note: This is an application to the A6 Hom carrier, with A3 quotient-by-torsion and R07.2 torsion faithfulness. It does not use p-tate-hom: its input is an already algebraic rational morphism, not an arbitrary local linear map.
items.proof: Write nα=h with n>0 and h an actual homomorphism. For each ℓ^a∥n, the lattice condition makes the realization of h divisible by ℓ^a. At ℓ≠p this kills A[ℓ^a] by étale torsion comparison. At p use the finite Dieudonné anti-equivalence, after linear duality, to conclude h kills A[p^a] as a group scheme. These primary subgroup schemes generate A[n], so h factors uniquely through [n] by its fppf quotient property. The factor equals α after rationalization. Apply the same argument to α^(−1) for the isomorphism assertion.
tests: For α=[1/ℓ], the lattice at ℓ detects nonintegrality even though every other local lattice is preserved.
At p an ordinary elliptic curve has a connected p-primary subgroup; geometric-point tests alone do not detect the full kernel condition.
An isogeny [ℓ] preserves each lattice by inclusion but does not carry the ℓ-lattice onto itself.

items.name: Finite-support lattice tuples are realized over the prime field
items.statement: Fix A₀/F_p. Let M_ℓ be full π-stable Z_ℓ-lattices in V_ℓ(A₀) for ℓ≠p and M_p a full F,V-stable Z_p-lattice in D^lin(A₀), equal to the reference realization lattices T₀,ℓ at all but finitely many primes. There exist B/F_p and a rational quasi-isogeny f:B→A₀ with transported realization lattices f_ℓ(T_ℓB)=M_ℓ, including D^lin at p.
items.locator: Waterhouse 1969 §§1.1–1.2 and lattice changes in Theorem 6.1; LT v1 §3 (5)–(6); continuation C4
items.note: This is essential surjectivity, using finite torsion subgroups and A3 quotients. It is not Waterhouse Proposition 3.1, which concerns conjugacy of algebra embeddings. Neither p-Tate full faithfulness nor unpolarized class finiteness is assumed.
items.proof: Choose N>0 with NT₀,ℓ⊆M_ℓ for every ℓ and put L_ℓ=N^(−1)M_ℓ⊇T₀,ℓ. At ℓ≠p, L_ℓ/T₀,ℓ gives a finite Galois-stable torsion subgroup. At p the annihilator L_p∨⊆C(A₀) gives the finite subgroup whose contravariant module is C(A₀)/L_p∨. Only finitely many are nonzero; combine the primary subgroup schemes to H⊂A₀ and form q:A₀→B=A₀/H. The exact torsion-realization comparisons give q_ℓ^(−1)(T₀,ℓ(B))=L_ℓ. The marking f=Nq^(−1) has image N L_ℓ=M_ℓ at every prime.
tests: The reference tuple is realized by B=A₀ and f=id.
For M_ℓ=ℓT₀,ℓ and all other components unchanged, N=ℓ produces the marking [ℓ], not [1/ℓ].
Infinitely many nontrivial components do not yield a finite subgroup H and are excluded.

items.name: Prime-field marked and unmarked classification
items.statement: For A₀/F_p, the transport map is a bijection from isomorphism classes of marked pairs (B,f:B→A₀ a rational quasi-isogeny) to the finite-support lattice tuples of prime-field-lattice-realization. Here (B,f)≅(B′,f′) means an F_p-isomorphism u:B→B′ with f′u=f. Under this bijection Γ=End⁰_Fp(A₀)^× acts by postcomposition, and Γ-orbits are precisely underlying F_p-isomorphism classes in the isogeny class of A₀.
items.note: This is the proved prime-field restriction of the existing general-q marked-quasi-isogeny and forget-marking targets; do not replace their general statements or claim their covariance problem is finished.
items.proof: Existence is prime-field-lattice-realization. For equal transported tuples, α=(f′)^(−1)f and its inverse preserve all integral realizations, so torsion-integrality-detection gives the unique marked isomorphism. Every rational marking differs from any other marking on the same object by postcomposition with an element of Γ. Conversely an equality up to this action gives an underlying isomorphism by the injectivity just proved.
tests: Changing f to af is the left Γ-action, not right multiplication on the source variety.
Two locally isomorphic lattice tuples need not lie in one rational Γ-orbit.
For the zero abelian variety the marked and unmarked sets are singletons.

items.name: Unique local orbit away from the minimal-polynomial discriminant
items.statement: Let γ be semisimple on a finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-space with monic squarefree minimal polynomial f∈Z_ℓ[T] and unit discriminant. Then R=Z_ℓ[γ] is finite étale and is its maximal order S=∏O_i. With V=⊕K_i^{n_i}, every full γ-stable Z_ℓ-lattice is a direct sum of free O_i-lattices of ranks n_i. The centralizer ∏GL_{n_i}(K_i) acts transitively, and its stabilizer is conjugate to ∏GL_{n_i}(O_i).
items.locator: LT v1 §3.1 integral-order setup; Waterhouse 1969 Theorem 6.1 good-prime step; continuation C5
items.note: Use the existing local-order and maximal-order carriers. This is a lattice adapter in GN.2. The discriminant is that of the squarefree minimal polynomial, never that of a characteristic polynomial with repeated factors. Finite-étale/maximal-order and local PID module interfaces remain implementation leaves.
items.proof: Invertible discriminant gives a finite étale Z_ℓ-algebra, a product of unramified DVRs, so R is the integral closure S. A γ-stable lattice is an R-module and decomposes by its integral idempotents; each torsion-free finite O_i-module is free. Choose bases and identify its stabilizer. All bases differ by the rational centralizer.
tests: For γ=aI on rank n, f=T−a has discriminant 1 for every n; the characteristic-polynomial discriminant is 0 for n>1 and is the wrong test.
For two distinct eigenvalues congruent modulo ℓ, the minimal discriminant is not a unit and the unique-orbit conclusion is not inferred.
D_*=1 gives a good local orbit at every prime for semisimple integral γ, but still need not give one rational isomorphism class.

items.name: Finite-support adelic stabilizers in a prime-field isogeny class
items.statement: For A₀/F_p and the prime-field lattice space X, use Tate full faithfulness at all primes to identify G(Q_ℓ), G=End⁰_Fp(A₀)^×, with the linear Frobenius centralizer. Let D_* be L8’s unequal-root-occurrence discriminant product. There is a compact open K₀=∏H₀,ℓ of G(A_f) such that every M∈X has Stab(M)=∏S_M,ℓ contained in a conjugate K_M=a_M K₀a_M^(−1), with a_M∈G(A_f) supported at finitely many places, S_M,ℓ=H_M,ℓ almost everywhere, and [K_M:Stab(M)]≤D_*. Moreover #G(A_f)\X≤D_*².
items.note: Specialized assembly consumes AA.1 restricted products, GN.2 good primes, S3 graded-profile stabilizers and S5 product indices. It does not invoke strong approximation or replace quaternionic groups by commutative ones. The p-Tate source leaf remains explicit.
items.proof: Outside p and the finitely many primes dividing disc(f_min), take H₀,ℓ=Stab(T₀,ℓ); good-prime-lattice-orbit identifies it with a product of integral GL groups. At the exceptional primes choose H₀,ℓ by S3 for the reference lattice. For a tuple M use the same group and conjugator 1 wherever M=T₀ and the prime is good; at the remaining finitely many places S3 supplies H_M,ℓ conjugate to H₀,ℓ and index at most ℓ^Δ_ℓ. These conjugators form an adele. Componentwise stabilization gives the product subgroup, and finite support makes it a subgroup of the restricted product. S5 and ∏ℓ^Δ_ℓ=D_* give the index. Local orbits multiply because there is just one good-prime orbit and conjugators can be chosen 1 outside finite support; the p F,V-stable subset is invariant under the same centralizer. L8 gives the D_*² bound.
tests: Repeated Frobenius factors do not make the exceptional set infinite: use f_min, not the full characteristic discriminant.
The chosen compact group comes from S3’s successive graded saturations, not from the saturation of the whole mixed lattice.
An arbitrary infinite sequence of local conjugators is not automatically an element of G(A_f).

items.name: Coarse prime-field isomorphism count at fixed adelic level
items.statement: For A₀/F_p of dimension g>0, put m=2g, take D_* and K₀ from prime-field-adelic-stabilizers, and suppose h=#(G(Q)\G(A_f)/K₀) is finite. Then the number of F_p-isomorphism classes in the isogeny class of A₀ is at most D_*³h≤(2√p)^{3m(m−1)}h. Class-set finiteness is imported from AA.3 with its exact group hypotheses; no numerical bound on h is included.
items.locator: LT v1 §§3.1.6–3.2.3; continuation C6, coarse replacement only
items.note: This applies the existing conditional-rational-orbit-bound after the prime-field arithmetic interfaces have been supplied. It is not the printed sharp coefficient, not an all-q result and not a reduced-norm or narrow-class-number comparison.

items.name: Prime-field p-realization Frobenius polynomial
items.statement: For A/F_p the linear Frobenius F on C(A)⊗Q_p, and hence its transpose on D^lin(A), is semisimple and has characteristic polynomial equal to the intrinsic degree-2dim(A) Frobenius polynomial P_A(T)∈Z[T] occurring on every V_ℓ(A), ℓ≠p.

items.statement: For a field K, a finite-dimensional simple K-algebra R, and a finite-dimensional K-vector space M with compatible R-action, dim_K End_R(M) · dim_K R = (dim_K M)^2. M may be zero; centrality of R is not required.

items.name: Exact finite-level contravariant Dieudonné comparison
items.statement: Over a perfect field k of characteristic p, the contravariant Dieudonné anti-equivalence on finite commutative p-primary group schemes is exact and faithful. For the p-divisible group of an abelian variety A, C(A)/p^n C(A) identifies naturally with D(A[p^n]); maps and short exact sequences have the reversed orientation.
items.locator: WM71 Part I Theorem 4, p.56; M68 §1, p.65.
items.note: Precise imported R07.2 interface, not a new Dieudonné category. The theorem statements were read in WM71/M68; the original Manin/Oda/Gabriel classification proofs cited there remain G8. Fix contravariance explicitly when adapting the existing dieudonne-lattice convention.

items.name: Dieudonné length measures group-scheme rank
items.statement: For a finite commutative p-primary group scheme H over a perfect field k, rank_k(H)=p^(length_W(k) D(H)). In particular the exponent uses p, including when k=F_(p^a); it does not use p^a or the number of geometric points of H.
items.locator: WM71 Part I Theorem 4, p.56; M68 §1, p.65.

items.name: Invariant of an unramified cyclic algebra
items.statement: For an unramified cyclic extension E/K of nonarchimedean local fields of degree n, let τ generate Gal(E/K), let φ be arithmetic Frobenius, and write φ=τ^r with gcd(r,n)=1. The cyclic algebra with Ua=τ(a)U and U^n=c∈K× has invariant r·ord_K(c)/n in Q/Z, with ord_K a uniformizer-normalized valuation.

The comparison from algebraic Brauer classes to cohomological classes must be retained. WM71 invokes the cocycle calculation without giving its full proof: that original supplier proof remains G8.

items.name: Dieudonné determinant detects the p-part of isogeny degree
items.statement: Let k=F_(p^a), W=W(k), L=Frac(W), and C be the contravariant realization. For an isogeny f:A→B, length_W coker C(f)=v_p(deg f). For an endomorphism isogeny f:A→A this also equals v_p(det_L(C(f)[1/p])), normalized by v_p(p)=1.
items.locator: M68 §1, p.65, determinant/length/degree comparison; WM71 Part I pp.56–57.
items.note: D-continuation: paper-specific application of existing carriers; source proof specified, no Lean implementation claimed.
items.proof: Decompose the finite kernel into its p-primary and prime-to-p parts using A3. Exact contravariance identifies coker C(f) with D((ker f)_p). Apply length/rank, and for an endomorphism use Smith normal form over the unramified DVR W to identify cokernel length with determinant valuation. The determinant statement is restricted to an endomorphism; no canonical determinant of a map between different spaces is asserted.
tests: For [p] on dimension g, all three quantities are 2g.
For a prime-to-p isogeny, the p-realization is an integral isomorphism and the length is zero.
Connected p-kernels are counted by scheme rank.

items.name: Characteristic polynomial on the p-realization
items.statement: For A/F_(p^a) and u∈End(A), the L-linear map C(u) on C(A)[1/p] has characteristic polynomial equal to the intrinsic polynomial P_u∈Z[X] of degree 2dim A, after mapping coefficients to L. This holds for arbitrary u without asserting that u is semisimple.
items.locator: M68 §1, pp.65–66; WM71 Part I p.57 and Part II p.60; handoff P1 expanded in report D1.
items.note: D-continuation: paper-specific application of existing carriers; source proof specified, no Lean implementation claimed. The V-continuation preserves this endpoint's statement and status, replacing its two generic audit placeholders by explicit pinned imports and missing implementation items.
items.proof: Writing F=Bσ, commutation gives T=Bσ(T)B^(-1), so the integral characteristic polynomial Q of T is σ-fixed and lies in Z_p[X]. For every integer ψ such that ψ(u) is an isogeny, the preceding valuation theorem gives v_p Res(Q,ψ)=v_p deg ψ(u)=v_p Res(P_u,ψ); the last equality is the A6 degree formula on V_ℓ and the determinant/resultant identity, not p-Tate. To separate monic P,Q∈Z_p[X], choose each monic irreducible factor R of PQ, choose monic integral R_n≡R mod p^(2n), and set ψ_n=R_n+p^n. Roots α of R have v_p ψ_n(α)=n, while at the other roots it is eventually v_p R(β). Thus the resultant valuation is n times the number of R-roots with multiplicities, plus a constant. Equality for large n gives all multiplicities, hence P=Q. Nonzero Res(P_u,ψ_n) ensures ψ_n(u) is an isogeny by A6, so these tests are admissible. Report D1 names the remaining generic adapter audits; Lang’s original uniqueness lemma is not claimed read. V1–V5 now supply the exact fixed-Witt-coefficient and resultant-recognition adapters. In V4 the separation proof instead uses the finite free quotient O[X]/(R), determinant congruences and monic Gauss lemma, so it no longer requires an extended valuation on a splitting field. V2 descends the integral characteristic polynomial even though the conjugating Frobenius matrix is invertible only after inverting p.
tests: A=0 gives polynomial 1.
For u=[[0,1],[0,0]] on E² the polynomial is X⁴; u need not be semisimple.
An irreducible factor R of degree d repeated e times contributes slope de to these resultant valuations.
When a>1 C(u) is L-linear, but F itself is only semilinear.

items.name: Semisimplicity of the linear q-Frobenius realization
items.statement: For A/F_(p^a), C(π_A)=F^a is an L-linear semisimple endomorphism of C(A)[1/p], where π_A is the q-power Frobenius. Its characteristic polynomial is P_A. No semisimplicity claim for arbitrary endomorphisms is included.
items.locator: M68 p.66, paragraph before Theorem 1; WM71 Part I p.57 and Part II p.60.
items.note: D-continuation: paper-specific application of existing carriers; source proof specified, no Lean implementation claimed.
items.proof: π_A is central in the finite-dimensional semisimple Q-algebra End⁰_k(A). Its minimal polynomial therefore has no repeated roots in characteristic zero. Functoriality transports this annihilating polynomial to C(π_A)=F^a, proving semisimplicity; use the independent polynomial comparison for the characteristic polynomial.
tests: Repeated isogeny factors may give repeated factors of P_A without destroying semisimplicity.
Over F_(p²) use F²; scalar Frobenius does not make F L-linear.
The zero realization is included.

items.name: Saturated injection on integral p-realization Hom groups
items.statement: For A,B/F_(p^a), the natural map j:Hom_k(A,B)⊗Z_p→Hom_(W,F,V)(C(B),C(A)) is injective with p-saturated image. This statement does not assume rational p-Tate or equality of ranks.
items.locator: WM71 Part I Theorems 3 and 5, pp.55–56, and saturation step p.57; expanded handoff P2/report D2.
items.note: D-continuation: paper-specific application of existing carriers; source proof specified, no Lean implementation claimed.
items.proof: The equivariant Hom module H is a finite torsion-free Z_p-submodule of the W-linear maps, and is p-saturated there by cancelling p in the F,V equations. A geometric homomorphism acting as zero modulo p therefore kills the group scheme A[p]. The quotient A/A[p]≅A given by [p] yields f=pg. Thus M/pM→H/pH is injective for M=Hom(A,B). For x∈M⊗Z_p in ker j, iterated reduction gives divisibility by every p-power, hence x=0. If j(x)=ph, reduction gives x=px′ and cancellation gives h=j(x′). All modules used are finite free over their stated DVR; no rank equality was used.
tests: Replacing A[p] by its geometric points would miss μ_p.
The same argument detects divisibility by p^n.
End is an anti-homomorphism; Hom has direction C(B)→C(A).

items.name: Algebra acting on a Frobenius polynomial block
items.statement: Let L/Q_p be unramified of degree a≥1 with arithmetic Frobenius σ, and let m∈Q_p[X] be monic irreducible with m(0)≠0. Put K=Q_p[X]/m and θ=X mod m. On ⊕_(0≤j<a)(L⊗Qp K)U^j define multiplication by U b=(σ⊗1)(b)U and U^a=θ. This defines a K-algebra B of dimension a². If a semilinear bijection F on an L-vector space V satisfies m(F^a)=0, the actions of L, θ↦F^a and U↦F define a B-module structure on V.
items.locator: WM71 Part II p.60 cyclic quotient and p.61 presentation; explicit finite-sum presentation of handoff P3.
items.note: Finite-field application in the existing Part II; reuse general tensor/direct-sum/central-simple APIs. This is not a second central-simple-algebra or Dieudonné category.
items.proof: Use the existing direct sum, tensor product and algebra carriers. For 0≤i,j<a set (bU^i)(cU^j)=bσ^i(c)θ^floor((i+j)/a)U^((i+j) mod a). Associativity follows from σ^a=1, σ(θ)=θ and the carry identity for residues modulo a. The basis count is a·dim_K(L⊗K)=a². The displayed relations verify the proposed module action; no general Ore-polynomial classification is assumed.

items.name: Central simplicity of a Frobenius block algebra
items.statement: The algebra B in p-frobenius-block-algebra is central simple over K. For an algebraic closure Ω/K, B⊗K Ω≅M_a(Ω). In particular the conclusion includes the cases where L⊗Qp K is a product of fields.
items.locator: WM71 Part II pp.60–61; weighted-cycle expansion of handoff P3/report D3.
items.note: D-continuation: paper-specific application of existing carriers; source proof specified, no Lean implementation claimed.
items.proof: Over Ω the étale coefficient algebra splits as Ω^a. Index its primitive idempotents so σ cyclically permutes them. Map these idempotents to diagonal matrix units and U to a cyclic permutation matrix with wrap weight θ. The a² matrices e_j U^r form the matrix-unit basis up to nonzero scalars, hence this is an algebra isomorphism. Descent of ideals and centers along a faithfully flat field extension gives central simplicity over K. The general descent statement belongs to the existing semisimple-algebra owner; its exact pinned adapter remains a named G8 audit obligation.

items.name: Dimension of the semilinear Frobenius commutant
items.statement: For A/F_(p^a), factor P_A=∏m_i^(e_i) over Q_p into distinct monic irreducibles of degrees d_i. For V=C(A)[1/p] and R=L[F,F^(-1)], dim_Qp End_R(V)=Σ_i d_i e_i².
items.locator: WM71 Part II Theorem 1 proof, pp.60–61; handoff P3/report D3.
items.note: D-continuation: paper-specific application of existing carriers; source proof specified, no Lean implementation claimed.
items.proof: The central semisimple F^a decomposes V into V_i killed by m_i(F^a); intertwiners between distinct i vanish by Bézout. Polynomial comparison gives dim_L V_i=d_i e_i and hence dim_Ki V_i=a e_i. Its R-endomorphisms are exactly its B_i-linear endomorphisms: B_i is generated by L and F. Apply the pinned dimension supplier to R=B_i, K=K_i and M=V_i: dim End_Bi(V_i)·a²=(ae_i)², so the dimension is e_i². Restrict scalars and sum. V=0 gives an empty sum. This uses the existing supplier instead of recreating a generic Morita/commutant-base-change library.

For F=σ on L² with a=2, the commutant over Q_p has dimension four, not eight.

items.name: Rational p-Tate comparison
items.statement: For A,B/F_(p^a), Hom_k(A,B)⊗Q_p→Hom_(L,F)(C(B)[1/p],C(A)[1/p]) is an isomorphism of Q_p-vector spaces. For A=B it identifies End⁰_k(A)^op⊗Q_p with the equivariant endomorphism algebra.
items.locator: WM71 Part II Theorem 1 proof, pp.60–61.
items.note: D-continuation: paper-specific application of existing carriers; source proof specified, no Lean implementation claimed.
items.proof: The saturated injection remains injective on rationalization. Prime-to-p Tate identifies dim_Q End⁰(A) with the semisimple Frobenius commutant dimension Σ d_i e_i²: compute after a common characteristic-zero splitting field, where each root contributes its multiplicity squared, to see independence of the local factorization. The p-realization commutant has that same dimension by the preceding item, giving the End anti-isomorphism. Apply to A×B and take off-diagonal projector corners, preserving contravariance. Every rational equivariant map becomes integral after multiplying by a power of p, so rationalization of integral H gives precisely this target.
tests: End is opposite, while the additive Hom comparison reverses source and target.
Off-diagonal corners of A×B supply Hom, not merely an equality of End dimensions.

items.name: Characteristic-prime invariant of a simple endomorphism algebra
items.statement: Let A/F_(p^a) be simple, with Frobenius π and center Q(π) of E=End⁰_k(A). For v|p put K=Q(π)_v, e_v=ord_v(p) and f_v its residue degree, with ord_v a uniformizer-normalized valuation. Then inv_v(E)=f_v ord_v(π)/a=[K:Q_p]ord_v(π)/ord_v(p^a) in Q/Z.
items.locator: WM71 Part II Theorem 2 and proof, pp.60–61; LT v1 Proposition 4.14(1).
items.note: D-continuation: paper-specific application of existing carriers; source proof specified, no Lean implementation claimed.
items.proof: Set g=gcd(f_v,a), n=a/g. The étale coefficient algebra L⊗Qp K has g factors E′=LK of degree n over K; the block algebra is M_g(D), with D generated over E′ by U, Uc=σ^g(c)U and U^n=π. This is the explicit matrix presentation on WM71 p.61. Arithmetic Frobenius of E′/K restricts to σ^(f_v), so equals (σ^g)^(f_v/g). The imported cyclic-invariant formula gives inv(D)=(f_v/g)ord_v(π)/(a/g)=f_v ord_v(π)/a. The faithful action of the central simple block inside End_K(V_v) and the tensor-centralizer theorem show the commutant has inverse Brauer class. Rational p-Tate identifies E_v^op with that commutant, so the second opposite reverses the sign again. Matrix algebras preserve the Brauer class. All-q p-Tate does not supply an all-q lattice-counting convention.
tests: At a=1 every finite p-invariant is zero, but real invariants may remain.
At a=3, f_v=1 and ord_v π=1 the invariant is 1/3, not 2/3.
If a=f_v=2 the coefficient tensor has two factors; pretending it is a field loses g.

items.name: A monic fraction-field factor has integral coefficients
items.statement: Let O be an integrally closed commutative domain and K its fraction field. If monic P∈O[X] has a divisor g∈K[X], there is g′∈O[X] with map(g′)·C(leadingCoeff g)=g. In particular, if g is monic it comes from a unique monic polynomial over O.

items.name: Frobenius-fixed Witt vectors are precisely p-adic constants
items.statement: For a field k of characteristic p and x∈W(k), F(x)=x iff there exists a unique z∈Z_p with ι_k(z)=x. Neither finiteness nor perfection of k is required.
items.locator: M68 §1, p.65, coefficient and polynomial uniqueness inputs; self-contained adapter proof in report V1–V5 (not an assertion that Lang VII §1 Lemma 1 was read).
items.note: Generic coefficient-recognition adapter on existing WittVector, Polynomial, AdjoinRoot and DVR carriers. Proof supplied here; no Lean implementation or independent verification claimed. Rerouted from the withdrawn LocalFieldsPartIICoefficientRecognition proposal to FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2. [cc-442dc5]
items.proof: Use coeff(Fx)_n=x_n^p and extensionality. Each coefficient of a fixed vector lies in the prime subfield by the pinned fixed-element theorem; lift it uniquely to F_p. Those lifted Witt coordinates define y∈W(F_p), with map(y)=x. Set z=equiv(y). Conversely prime-field Witt Frobenius is the identity. Injectivity gives uniqueness. Use Witt coordinates, not ghost coordinates.

items.name: Integral characteristic polynomial descends along Witt Frobenius
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W=W(k), L=Frac(W), σ the extended Witt Frobenius, T a square matrix over W, and B an invertible matrix over L. If T_L=B·σ(T_L)·B⁻¹, there is a unique monic P∈Z_p[X] whose coefficient image under ι_k is charpoly_W(T). Its degree equals the matrix size, including size zero.
items.locator: M68 §1, p.65, coefficient and polynomial uniqueness inputs; self-contained adapter proof in report V1–V5 (not an assertion that Lang VII §1 Lemma 1 was read).
items.note: Generic coefficient-recognition adapter on existing WittVector, Polynomial, AdjoinRoot and DVR carriers. Proof supplied here; no Lean implementation or independent verification claimed. Rerouted from the withdrawn LocalFieldsPartIICoefficientRecognition proposal to FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2. [cc-442dc5]
items.proof: Conjugation invariance and scalar-map compatibility give σ(charpoly_L T_L)=charpoly_L T_L. Since W→L is injective, each coefficient of charpoly_W T is fixed by Witt Frobenius. Apply the fixed-ring theorem coefficientwise; injectivity gives the unique polynomial, with monicity and degree preserved. Only B is required invertible over L, not over W; no semisimplicity of T is used.

items.name: Monic polynomial lifting at an ideal-power precision
items.statement: Let O be a DVR with uniformizer π and let ι:D→O be a homomorphism of commutative rings whose composites D→O/(π^N) are surjective for every N≥1. For every monic f∈O[X] and N≥1 there is monic g∈D[X] of the same degree such that every coefficient of map(ι,g)−f lies in (π^N).
items.locator: M68 §1, p.65, coefficient and polynomial uniqueness inputs; self-contained adapter proof in report V1–V5 (not an assertion that Lang VII §1 Lemma 1 was read).
items.note: The general proof uses the displayed quotient-surjectivity hypothesis; PadicInt.appr is needed only for the Z→Z_p specialization, not as a hypothesis on arbitrary O. No completeness or finite residue field is assumed. Rerouted from the withdrawn LocalFieldsPartIICoefficientRecognition proposal to the finite-field Part II, its only consumer. [cc-442dc5]
items.proof: Choose a representative in D for each of the finitely many nonleading coefficients and fix the leading coefficient to 1. Higher coefficients are zero. The map is to a nonzero ring, so D is nonzero; monicity and degree are literal, not merely upper bounds. For f=1 choose g=1.

items.name: Resultant respects congruence in the second polynomial
items.statement: Let O be a commutative ring, I an ideal, S∈O[X] monic, and G,H∈O[X] coefficientwise congruent modulo I. Then Res(S,G)−Res(S,H)∈I, with each resultant interpreted at actual degrees.
items.locator: M68 §1, p.65, coefficient and polynomial uniqueness inputs; self-contained adapter proof in report V1–V5 (not an assertion that Lang VII §1 Lemma 1 was read).
items.note: Generic coefficient-recognition adapter on existing WittVector, Polynomial, AdjoinRoot and DVR carriers. Proof supplied here; no Lean implementation or independent verification claimed. Rerouted from the withdrawn LocalFieldsPartIICoefficientRecognition proposal to the finite-field Part II, its only consumer. [cc-442dc5]
items.proof: Use the quotient map O→O/I and the same bound max(deg G,deg H) on both second polynomials. The pinned monic padding lemma changes both resultants to that bound. Coefficientwise congruence makes the second polynomials equal after quotient. Base change of the Sylvester determinant proves equality of the images, hence the ideal membership. Alternatively use multiplication matrices on O[X]/(S). If I=O the assertion is immediate; otherwise the monic first polynomial keeps its degree after reduction.

items.name: A shifted approximate factor detects its multiplicity
items.statement: Let O be a DVR, π a uniformizer, K=Frac(O), R∈O[X] monic of positive degree d and irreducible over K. Write monic P=R^e S in O[X], where R does not divide S in K[X]. For n≥1 let ψ_n∈O[X] be congruent coefficientwise to R+π^n modulo π^(2n). Put c=v(Res(S,R)), finite because R,S are coprime over K. For every n>c, Res(P,ψ_n)≠0 and v(Res(P,ψ_n))=n d e+c, with v(π)=1.
items.locator: M68 §1, p.65, coefficient and polynomial uniqueness inputs; self-contained adapter proof in report V1–V5 (not an assertion that Lang VII §1 Lemma 1 was read).
items.note: Generic coefficient-recognition adapter on existing WittVector, Polynomial, AdjoinRoot and DVR carriers. Proof supplied here; no Lean implementation or independent verification claimed. Rerouted from the withdrawn LocalFieldsPartIICoefficientRecognition proposal to the finite-field Part II, its only consumer. [cc-442dc5]
items.proof: In the free rank-d ring O[X]/(R), multiplication by ψ_n is π^n(I+π^nM_n). Its determinant is π^(nd) times a unit: reduction of I+π^nM_n is the identity. The pinned norm–resultant identity yields v Res(R,ψ_n)=nd. Congruence of ψ_n with R modulo π^n gives Res(S,ψ_n)≡Res(S,R) mod π^n; when n>c their valuations equal c. Multiplicativity gives the result. S=1 gives c=0 and e=0 is allowed.

tests.name: resultant_slope_degree_weight
tests.statement: Over Z_3, R=X²+1, P=R^e and ψ_n=R+3^n give v_3 Res(P,ψ_n)=2ne.

tests.name: resultant_slope_coprime_block
tests.statement: Over Z_3 take R=X, S=X−3, e=2 and ψ_n=X+3^n. For n>1 the valuation is 2n+1.

tests.name: resultant_slope_precision_needed
tests.statement: Congruence only modulo π^n permits ψ_n=R, giving a zero resultant; the 2n accuracy cannot be silently weakened.

tests.name: resultant_slope_no_divisor

items.name: Monic polynomials are determined by nonzero resultant valuations
items.statement: Let O be a DVR with fraction field K and uniformizer π. Let ι:D→O be a commutative-ring homomorphism surjective modulo every (π^N), N≥1. If P,Q∈O[X] are monic and v Res(P,map ι ψ)=v Res(Q,map ι ψ) for every monic ψ∈D[X] for which both resultants are nonzero, then P=Q. Equal degree, completeness, separability, characteristic zero and finiteness of the residue field are not extra hypotheses.
items.locator: M68 §1, p.65, coefficient and polynomial uniqueness inputs; self-contained adapter proof in report V1–V5 (not an assertion that Lang VII §1 Lemma 1 was read).
items.note: Generic coefficient-recognition adapter on existing WittVector, Polynomial, AdjoinRoot and DVR carriers. Proof supplied here; no Lean implementation or independent verification claimed. Rerouted from the withdrawn LocalFieldsPartIICoefficientRecognition proposal to the finite-field Part II, its only consumer. [cc-442dc5]
items.proof: Factor P and Q into monic irreducibles over K. Each factor and each monic complementary factor lies in O[X] by the pinned Gauss lemma. For each nonconstant factor R of PQ, lift R+π^n monically to ψ_n∈D[X] modulo π^(2n) using quotient-surjectivity. The factor-slope theorem applied separately to P,Q makes both resultants nonzero for all sufficiently large n and gives nd e_P+c_P=nd e_Q+c_Q. Subtract at consecutive sufficiently large n to obtain d e_P=d e_Q; d>0 implies equal exponents. Monicity removes the final unit ambiguity. This includes P=1 or Q=1.

items.name: DiPippo–Howe lower bound for isogeny classes
items.locator: Remark 2.3; [6] DiPippo–Howe, J. Number Theory 73 (1998), Theorem 1.3 (arXiv:math/9803097v3, p.2)
items.statement: For every positive integer n and prime power q, the number #O(q,n) of isogeny classes of ordinary n-dimensional abelian varieties over F_q satisfies #O(q,n) > c_4 (c_5 n)^(−2 log 2/log q) (2^n/n!) (r(q) q^(n/2) − n) q^(n(n−1)/4), where c_4 = e^(−3/2), c_5 = 2+√2 and r(q) = φ(q)/q. Hence, with Lemma 2.1 corrected, the logarithm of the number of isogeny classes of g-dimensional abelian varieties over F_q is (1/4)g² log q (1+o(1)) as g→∞, for every fixed q.
items.note: Read at the source (arXiv v3, the corrected version of the published paper). LT say this certifies Corollary 2.2 over prime fields and only "suspect" it over F_(p^r); Theorem 1.3 holds for every q, so the hedge is unnecessary (not recorded as an error). Routed to the finite-field Part II with Corollary 2.2. [cc-442dc5]

items.name: A positive involution of a CM field is complex conjugation
items.locator: §4.5 before Proposition 4.16 and its proof; [19, §21] (Albert's classification)
items.statement: Let L be a CM field and x ↦ x′ an involution of L that is positive, i.e. Tr_(L/Q)(x x′) > 0 for all x ≠ 0. Then ′ is the complex conjugation of L. In particular, if A is a simple abelian variety with End⁰(A) a CM field, every Rosati involution of A is complex conjugation.
items.note: The paper uses only this case of Albert's classification. Proof: the fixed field F of ′ has positive definite trace form, so F is totally real; ′ ≠ id because L is not totally real; and the only automorphism of a CM field with totally real fixed field of index 2 is complex conjugation. Routed to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6 (Rosati positivity). [cc-442dc5]

items.name: Hasse norm theorem for cyclic extensions
items.statement: For a cyclic extension L/K of number fields, x ∈ K^× is a norm from L^× if and only if it is a local norm at every place of K.
items.note: Planned as cyclicHasseNorm and isGlobalNorm_iff_isLocalNormEverywhere in Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 13; not in Tau Ceti at f790474 (searched). Used for (31). [cc-442dc5]

items.name: Units that are norms modulo norms of units (Lemmermeyer)
items.statement: Let L/K be a cyclic extension of number fields of prime degree. There is an exact sequence 1 → Am_st(L/K) → Am(L/K) → (E_K ∩ N_(L/K)L^×)/N_(L/K)E_L → 1, where Am(L/K) ⊂ Cl(L) is the group of ambiguous ideal classes and Am_st(L/K) its subgroup of strongly ambiguous classes. In particular (E_K ∩ N L^×)/N E_L is a subquotient of Cl(L) and its order is at most h(L).
items.note: Read at the source (Lemmermeyer's Proposition 1, proved with Hilbert 90 for ideals). Used in (31) for L/K a CM extension. Routed to the finite-field Part II, whose polarization count consumes it. [cc-442dc5]

items.name: Hasse principle for hermitian forms (Landherr)
items.statement: Let L/K be a quadratic extension of number fields. Two nondegenerate hermitian forms over L (with respect to L/K) that are isometric over L⊗K_v for every place v of K are isometric over L.
items.note: Planned: GN.2 plans Hasse–Minkowski with "quaternionic/hermitian variants". gram-orbit-bijection consumes it. [cc-442dc5]

items.name: Lang's theorem over finite fields
items.statement: Let G be a smooth connected algebraic group over a finite field k. Then H^1(k, G) = 0. Consequently, for an exact sequence 1 → G′ → G → G″ → 1 of smooth algebraic k-groups with G′ connected, G(k) → G″(k) is surjective.
items.note: The paper applies it to 1 → SU_σ → U_σ → U_h → 1 over the residue field. No pinned declaration (Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 searched for Lang/Lang–Steinberg) and no atlas layer plans it. Routed as a source of ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3, whose smooth connected special fibres and reduction maps need it. [cc-442dc5]
